Released-file and full-package ZIP downloads retain their attempt and outcome. Only a complete successful transfer counts toward the retention condition. Partial downloads, failures, cancellations, and timeouts do not count. Older download records without verified completion remain in history and do not become successful downloads merely because the record exists. Governed PSeq packages use the same frozen policy and verified-download rules. Downloads obey their deadline independently of cleanup, and existing schedules retain their original dates. Automated notices and physical file deletion depend on the enabled retention services. Check the receipt for their recorded outcomes; a closed download window does not prove that files were deleted.

sections.heading: Accounting and recovery
sections.text: Use Order Ops → Finance for native PSeq invoices, receipts, allocations, imports, aging and reconciliation. Export reports from the owning Finance view. An export does not record payment or mark an invoice as posted elsewhere. Historical connector mappings and explicit QuickBooks catalog recovery remain in Legacy links. A queued recovery request does not prove that the connector is configured or that the catalog synchronized. An unconfigured connector reports unavailable and Needs attention; it records no invoice, payment, or successful balance. The active Service catalog can be maintained directly. Consult the owning integration recovery status before retrying a historical connector operation.

sections.heading: Activate production dependencies
sections.text: Before production use, confirm approved storage and malware scanning, notification delivery, active catalog and scientific profiles, Partner offerings and prices, applicable Partner credit decisions, quote validity, Finance responsibility, and operational ownership. Laboratory activation also requires approved bench workflows, label/printer/scanner and degraded-mode procedures, external NGS provider operating details, and approved operating procedures. Use only the equipment, destinations, and procedures authorized for real work.

sections.heading: Recover a retention notice
sections.text: Filter Owned attention queues to Retention notices. An urgent item identifies the package, deadline, and notification requiring recovery. Confirm active Organization administrators, correct the delivery issue, and retry the existing notification. A later grace notice uses the original final date. Resolution does not extend retention or confirm physical deletion; a persisting delivery failure can reopen the item.

sections.heading: Preserve a release or record a reissue
sections.text: A Phaeno platform administrator can open File retention → Review released packages, find the organization, and open a package's retained receipt. The detail page shows its full manifest, checksums, original retention dates, download evidence, cleanup outcome and reissue history. Use Print / save PDF for a metadata copy. A historical release may lack captured sample lineage; do not infer missing facts. Choose Place hold, select the hold type, and record the reason. Preserve bytes blocks physical cleanup. Quarantine and suspend access also stops current transfers and blocks new downloads; it is available only where download monitoring is active. Neither action resets retention. Hold reasons remain in the Phaeno management view rather than the external receipt. Use Release hold with a reason when preservation is no longer needed. If the original deadline has passed, cleanup may proceed once every hold is released and active transfer leases have ended. A stale-record error refreshes the details and preserves your entered reason; review the current state before retrying. After deletion, first regenerate and approve a new package through the owning scientific workflow. Then open the old receipt and choose Link reissued package, select the eligible new release, and record the authorization reason. POMS requires the same organization, workflow and sample where applicable, new file objects, and a release created after the original deletion. Linking never restores deleted bytes or changes the original release dates. Cleanup can remain pending for active transfers, preservation, shared source files, an incomplete package, or provider failure. Provider failures are retried against the same objects. Files deleted records successful physical cleanup; Downloads closed alone does not. Escalate repeated failures with the package reference and safe status, without copying credentials or scientific files.

guides.title: Customer relationship management
guides.summary: Manage canonical Companies, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, Portal access, Tasks, reporting, and data quality.

sections.heading: Customer relationship management
sections.text: The POMS CRM is Phaeno's first-party commercial and customer system of record. It runs without HubSpot or another external CRM and retains Companies, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, Activities, Tasks, pipeline history, reporting, Portal access, and reviewed handoffs in POMS. CRM records are internal Phaeno records. The Company is the canonical Customer, Partner, or Prospect identity. Creating it does not grant membership, activate a service, authorize ordering, start laboratory work, or expose scientific data.

sections.heading: Access CRM
sections.text: Open CRM from the Phaeno toolbar. CRM access requires an active Phaeno platform-administrator account. External organization users cannot see CRM navigation or CRM data. Use the far-left sidebar beneath the toolbar to move among the complete CRM workspace. Relationships contains Companies and Contacts; Sales contains Leads and Opportunities; Follow-up contains Tasks and Requests; Insights contains Reports; and Administration contains CRM configuration. Home remains the starting summary. The sidebar header identifies CRM and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar from the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the edge tab. Choosing a section closes an unpinned sidebar.

sections.heading: Start from Home
sections.text: Home answers what needs attention. It shows overdue and due-soon Tasks, Leads without a next action, stale Opportunities, required-data warnings, your next Tasks, and recently changed Opportunities. Use Find anything to search active Companies, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, and Tasks. Enter at least two characters, then choose a result to open its owning workspace. Search does not cross into Portal users, specimens, files, or laboratory records.

sections.heading: Keep the domain boundaries clear
sections.text: CRM owns the canonical Company, commercial relationship facts, qualification, pursuits, follow-up, sales history, and the central Requests review queue. Company detail presents the internal tenant scope, memberships, invitations, readiness, and service entitlements after Portal access is enabled. That scope is not a second customer record. Order operations owns commercial orders, quotes, cancellation and hold decisions, Finance, and governed result publication. Lab operations owns physical fulfillment, laboratory execution, and scientific approval. Lab operations owns physical specimens, accession, controlled execution, materials, equipment, libraries, batches, sendouts, exceptions, and scientific approval. Use a reviewed CRM handoff when relationship context should enable or change Portal access or enter Order operations. Never copy patient information, sample identifiers, scientific results, credentials, confidential file contents, or internal laboratory investigation notes into CRM. Use the CRM subtopics in this guide for complete field, status, workflow, administration, handoff, and recovery instructions.

guides.title: Activities and Tasks
guides.summary: Record commercial interactions and manage owned, recurring follow-up in record context.

sections.heading: Activities and Tasks
sections.text: Company, Contact, Lead, and Opportunity workspaces contain one commercial activity timeline and a linked Task list. Record work in the owning record so its context remains visible.

sections.heading: Log an Activity
sections.text: Select Log activity from the record workspace. Choose Note, Call, Meeting, Email, or Status change; enter the required subject and optional details. POMS records the current time and signed-in actor. Choose visibility deliberately: Internal is ordinary Phaeno commercial context. Restricted flags material requiring careful handling. It does not limit visibility to a smaller set of CRM administrators; every user with CRM access can read the activity. Keep confidential procedures and scientific evidence in their authorized owning system. Manually logged Email means a user recorded that an email occurred. It does not send or retrieve email. Connected email and calendar capture are deferred. System, Portal, and Task events may also appear in the timeline. They are written by POMS and cannot be edited as ordinary notes. Never place patient information, sample identifiers, credentials, scientific results, file contents, or laboratory investigation detail in an Activity.

sections.heading: Create a Task
sections.text: Select New task from the owning record. A title is required. Add a description, active Phaeno owner, priority, due date and time, reminder, and optional daily, weekly, or monthly recurrence. Priorities are Low, Normal, High, and Urgent. Use them to communicate commercial urgency, not scientific or patient severity. A Task must be linked to a Company, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity; the standalone Tasks workspace intentionally does not create context-free Tasks.

sections.heading: Manage the Task queue
sections.text: Open Tasks from the CRM sidebar to search by title or description, filter by status or overdue state, page through results, apply saved views, and export the current view. Search and filters remain when you return from a record. Statuses are: Open: not started. In progress: actively owned. Blocked: unable to proceed; a reason is required. Completed: finished. Cancelled: intentionally stopped. Use Update to change status. A blocked Task requires the blocking reason. Completed and Cancelled Tasks retain their history and no longer offer Update. Create a new follow-up Task when more work is needed. Completing a recurring Task creates its next occurrence according to the stored rule. Confirm the new occurrence and due date rather than changing the completed historical Task.

sections.heading: Use Home attention safely
sections.text: CRM Home shows overdue Tasks, Tasks due within seven days, and your next assigned Tasks. Completing a Task from Home uses the same durable status transition as the record workspace. If the Task has changed since Home loaded, refresh before retrying so a newer owner's work is not overwritten.

guides.title: Companies and Contacts
guides.summary: Maintain Company identity, contextual People, relationships, invitations, and Portal access in one workspace.

sections.heading: Companies and People
sections.text: Companies and Contacts are durable relationship records. The Company is also the canonical Customer, Partner, or Prospect identity. A Company does not become accessible to external users until Portal access is reviewed and enabled; a Contact never becomes a Portal user automatically.

sections.heading: Create and find a Company
sections.text: Open Companies from the CRM sidebar. Search by the known organization identity and review possible duplicates before selecting New company. Company name is required; Website and relationship stage remain visible for quick entry. Open Additional details only when you need to record: an explicit normalized domain; when left blank, POMS derives it from Website source, industry, employee count, phone, and postal address tags and a relationship summary Company, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, and Task lists show total counts and pages. Searches update after a short pause; Clear all resets active filters. Opening a record and using its Back link retains the list search, filters, and page. Company sections remain in the URL. POMS assigns the creator as owner unless another supported owner is selected later. The Company name opens a stable, view-first workspace. Use Overview for the Company profile and custom data, People for Contacts and Portal identity/access state, Sales for Opportunities, Departments & services for approved operational access and configuration, Requests for request creation and history, and Activity for the commercial timeline and Tasks. Use CRM's central Requests queue for approve, decline, recovery, application, and completion decisions. Changing a CRM lifecycle to Active customer or Partner is descriptive only. It does not enable or reclassify Portal access, grant membership, activate services, or authorize orders.

sections.heading: Create and manage a Contact
sections.text: From a Company’s People section, select New person to create the Contact and its Company association together. The global Contacts directory also provides New contact when no Company context is available. First name and last name are required. Record email, phone, Phaeno owner, tags, and the communication controls that apply: Unknown means permission has not been established. Permitted means the recorded commercial basis permits contact. Opted out records a preference not to receive the applicable communication. Do not contact is the strongest operational stop. Record the lawful-contact basis and communication notes when known. These fields are commercial compliance context, not legal advice and not a substitute for any required campaign-specific consent process. A Contact is not a Portal user. Email equality does not link identities, issue an invitation, or grant access. From a Company’s People section, use Invite to Portal for a reviewed Contact and choose Organization-administrator or explicit Department access. Manage access provides role changes, Department access, membership deactivation, and invitation resend/revoke. Successful acceptance creates the Portal membership and the explicit Contact/User identity link. If POMS finds an existing Portal user with the same email, it shows Identity review; select Review and link, verify that both records identify the same person, and record the reason. Never treat the suggestion as proof. Unlinked Portal users and invitations remain visible until staff intentionally resolve them.

sections.heading: Associate Contacts and Companies
sections.text: Open either record workspace to create the association: use Add existing person in the Company's People section to search incrementally for an existing Contact, or use Associate in the Contact's Company relationships area to search incrementally for an existing Company. Record the Contact's free-form job title at that Company and choose the relationship role—Decision maker, Scientific lead, Procurement, Executive sponsor, Champion, Influencer, Technical evaluator, or Other—then record whether this is the Contact's primary Company and the effective-from date. A Contact may be associated with more than one Company, with a different title and relationship role at each. Job title and relationship role are intentionally different. Job title is the person's organization-specific position, such as Director of Genomics, and remains free-form. Relationship role describes how the person participates in the commercial relationship and uses the controlled choices above. The Contacts directory displays the title and Company from the active primary relationship. Each relationship remains visible from the Company's People section and the Contact's Company relationships card. When a title, role, primary designation, or effective date changes, edit the Company relationship rather than the Contact's identity. When a relationship ends, record an effective-to date. Do not delete the Contact or overwrite the former Company simply to hide historical employment. POMS retains the effective-dated relationship and marks ended rows consistently in both workspaces.

sections.heading: Deactivate, reactivate, and merge
sections.text: Deactivate a Company or Contact when it should leave active directories while its history remains available. Reactivation restores the same CRM identity. Deactivating a Company suspends its attached Portal access scope; reactivating restores it. Contact lifecycle actions do not change Portal users. Use Merge only for a confirmed duplicate: Open the duplicate record that should be retired. Choose the record that should remain authoritative. Record a required merge reason. Review the consequence and confirm. POMS retains the source as an inactive alias, moves supported relationships and history, and writes a permanent merge record. If only one Company has Portal access, that access scope follows the surviving Company. POMS blocks a merge when both Companies have Portal access because choosing the surviving tenant requires an explicit data decision. Ordinary CRM UI does not undo a merge. If the records describe different legal entities or people, do not merge them; correct their fields or effective-dated relationships instead.

sections.heading: Complete required custom data
sections.text: Active custom fields configured for Company or Contact appear in the record workspace; Company custom fields are under Overview. Option fields accept only configured choices. A missing required value is shown on the record and contributes to CRM Home data-quality warnings. Complete the value on the authoritative record rather than suppressing the warning with unrelated text.

sections.heading: Create an Opportunity from its Company
sections.text: Open Sales and select New opportunity. The shared Opportunity form retains this Company, so you can capture the pursuit without leaving its workspace. The resulting record appears in Company Sales and the global Opportunity list.

guides.title: Leads and conversion
guides.summary: Capture signals, record qualification decisions, and convert without granting Portal access.

sections.heading: Leads and conversion
sections.text: Use a Lead for an unqualified commercial signal that is not yet ready to become a durable Company, Contact, or Opportunity.

sections.heading: Capture the Lead
sections.text: Open Leads and select New lead. Choose Individual or Company and enter the required display name. A Company Lead also requires a company name. Add contact facts, source, owner, next action, and tags when known. Do not create a Contact merely because an email address arrived, and do not create a Company merely because a web domain was observed. The Lead preserves the original signal while qualification is incomplete. Lead statuses are: New: captured but not yet worked. Working: active follow-up has begun. Qualified: the signal is suitable for conversion. Disqualified: the signal will not proceed; the reason is retained. Converted: the selected CRM records were created or linked and the original Lead is immutable history. Use status and search filters to find the relevant queue. Save a view when the same filter supports recurring work.

sections.heading: Qualify or disqualify
sections.text: Open the Lead. Select Start working before active follow-up when it is still New. Qualification and disqualification require an explanation so another Phaeno user can understand the decision. The full-width Qualification record shows only the applicable decision: qualification notes for Qualified or Converted Leads, the disqualification reason for Disqualified Leads, or a concise pending state while no decision exists. Qualify only when the organization or person, commercial fit, and next action are understood well enough to avoid speculative records. Disqualify when follow-up should stop; record the actual commercial reason without protected scientific or patient information.

sections.heading: Convert a qualified Lead
sections.text: Select Convert lead only from a Qualified Lead. Review each requested result: link an existing Company or create a Company from the Lead optionally create a Contact optionally create an Opportunity in an active pipeline If an existing Company is chosen, POMS links conversion to that CRM identity. If a new Company is requested, the Company name is required. Opportunity creation requires the Company outcome and uses the selected or default active pipeline. Likely Company or Contact duplicates stop unsafe creation or are returned as warnings. Review the suggested records and retry with an existing authoritative identity when appropriate. Do not alter spelling or identifying data merely to bypass duplicate detection. Conversion records the resulting Company, Contact, and Opportunity identifiers on the original Lead. It never enables Portal access or creates a user, entitlement, order, shipment, or Lab work order.

sections.heading: Correct mistakes safely
sections.text: Converted and Disqualified Leads are terminal for ordinary editing. Preserve them as decision history. If commercial work later resumes, use the resulting records or create a new Lead that represents the genuinely new signal; do not rewrite the old decision. If a save reports stale data, reload the Lead, review the newer change, and submit a deliberate update. If conversion partially appears to have succeeded, refresh the Lead and open its recorded conversion results before retrying.

guides.title: Opportunities and pipelines
guides.summary: Run commercial pursuits through controlled stages, immutable history, and currency-safe reporting.

sections.heading: Opportunities and pipelines
sections.text: An Opportunity represents one commercial pursuit for one CRM Company. It is not an order, quote, entitlement, or promise that Phaeno will perform work.

sections.heading: Create an Opportunity
sections.text: Open Opportunities and select New opportunity. Record the required Opportunity name, Company, and active pipeline. POMS assigns a unique, read-only Opportunity Number when the record is created, starts the Opportunity in the selected initial stage, and records the first stage-history entry. Use the Opportunity Number when referring to the pursuit outside its detail workspace. Product interest is optional and uses the defined PSeq Lab Service or PSeq Kit product domain rather than free text. You may also record: Phaeno owner and product or service interest amount and three-letter currency expected close date, next step, competitors, description, and tags Amount remains in its recorded currency. POMS does not silently convert it. Keep the next step current so Home and reporting can distinguish active work from stale work.

sections.heading: Work the pipeline
sections.text: The default board groups Opportunities by active stage. Use Table view when comparison across Company, stage, amount, close date, and owner is more useful. Search by identity and filter by pipeline or stage. Saved views retain the current filters and board/table choice; Export current view uses those same filters. Open the Opportunity name for its view-first workspace. Use Edit for commercial facts. Associate buying-team Contacts with an optional role and one primary Contact when that reflects the pursuit.

sections.heading: Move stages deliberately
sections.text: Use Move stage from the Opportunity workspace. Select another active stage from the same pipeline and record the required reason or useful context. Stages are categorized as Open, Won, Lost, or Abandoned and carry the configured probability. A configured stage may require a reason. Lost and Abandoned stages in the default pipeline require outcome context. POMS rejects a move to a stage from another pipeline or an invalid terminal transition. Every accepted transition writes immutable history containing the prior stage, new stage, actor, time, and reason. Moving a closed Opportunity back to an Open stage clears the current closed outcome while retaining earlier history. Do not edit pipeline configuration to falsify one Opportunity's outcome. Correct the Opportunity through a valid stage transition and leave the historical transition visible.

sections.heading: Interpret values and reports
sections.text: Counts include Opportunities in every currency. Aggregate amount and weighted-forecast figures are USD-only; a non-USD Opportunity is counted but its amount is not treated as converted USD. Probability is taken from the active stage for reporting. An Opportunity marked Won is still only commercial evidence. Use a reviewed CRM handoff for Portal onboarding, evaluation, Trial Project, custom work, service change, relationship change, or offboarding. Orders and Lab work retain their separate authorization gates.

guides.title: Company requests and approvals
guides.summary: Create Company requests, decide them centrally, complete approved work, and apply reviewed Prospect conversions.

sections.heading: Company requests and approvals
sections.text: A Company request carries commercial context into an audited review queue. It can propose online access, products and services, a relationship change, or reviewed work without creating another customer identity.

sections.heading: Create a Company request
sections.text: Open the CRM Company, select Requests, and then select Create request. Start with What does this Company need?: Online access: onboarding, evaluation, or offboarding Products and services: service change Work: Trial Project or custom work Relationship: relationship change The form asks for a more specific request type only when the selected outcome has more than one. It then shows only fields relevant to that request. For new online access, choose Prospect, Customer, or Partner. Requests for an existing relationship show its current kind. An existing Prospect can use Change the relationship to request Customer or Partner; the selected target is preserved for review. Link an Opportunity when evaluation or work arose from a specific commercial pursuit; Customer order handoffs still begin from the Opportunity workspace. An Online access request never asks for a product or service. It creates or changes the Company's sign-in scope, and users can reach only the products and services the Company is separately entitled to use. Choose Products and services and Service change when product or ordering eligibility must change. Add a relationship summary suitable for the affected Company only when the reviewer needs more context; POMS supplies a short request label when the summary is blank. Do not include patient information, sample identifiers, scientific results, credentials, confidential file contents, or laboratory investigation detail. The handoff summary is relationship context for review, not an unrestricted notes field.

sections.heading: Understand what is created
sections.text: Submitting creates one pending Company request with a retained operation identity. It appears in CRM's Requests review queue and, when applicable, Order operations intake. The Company workspace shows the request number, type, status, and creation time. The handoff does not by itself: enable or reclassify Portal access invite or activate a user mark the Company Ready activate a service entitlement or ordering authorization create a quote, order, sample roster, shipment, or Lab work order approve offboarding or revoke existing access An authorized reviewer owns those consequences in the destination workflow. Online access is one possible request outcome, not the parent of every request. When onboarding or evaluation is approved, POMS attaches one internal tenant scope to the existing Company. That access scope keeps the Company's records and sign-in rights separate; it is not another Company or customer identity and does not add or remove any product or service entitlement.

sections.heading: Review and follow up
sections.text: Open CRM's central Requests section to review onboarding, evaluation, products and services, relationship, work, or offboarding requests. Use Needs decision for pending review, Approved / needs work for fulfillment and access recovery, and Completed / history for finished decisions. The Company's Requests tab keeps history and links both pending and approved items to the same queue. After performing the approved work, select Complete request and record what was completed. For an approved relationship change, Apply Customer relationship or Apply Partner relationship performs the Prospect conversion and completes the request in one action. Open Order operations for custom-work or order-intake review when the request is applicable there. Keep CRM Activities and Tasks focused on commercial follow-up; record each decision in its owning workflow. For Customer PSeq Lab Service, a Won Opportunity can create a dedicated Customer order handoff from its detail page. After Company request review approves the request and confirms the active Company operational scope, Ready ordering entitlement, available service offering, and no manual operational block, Start Customer order appears in both the Opportunity and Order intake. An online Customer administrator is not required to begin pricing, but every non-billing readiness item and an active administrator are required before the quote can be issued. Billing readiness may be completed after acceptance and must be complete before invoicing. Starting the order creates one order, marks the request Applied in the same transaction, and links both records. Open the resulting order from either surface. Create a separate reviewed handoff when the same Opportunity legitimately produces another order; never retry by creating a duplicate handoff. Trial Project and Portal Evaluation handoffs do not start Customer orders. Company-level Customer order handoffs may start an order without an Opportunity, but they follow the same approval and eligibility checks. If the Company already has active online access, choose the appropriate change or offboarding request instead of creating a second onboarding request. If a submission outcome is uncertain, check Company request history before creating another request. A repeated operation key is rejected as an existing handoff. CRM lifecycle labels and Opportunity Won status never substitute for this reviewed boundary.

sections.heading: Trial Project handoff
sections.text: Create a Trial Project request from an active Company Opportunity. Its request carries commercial context; scientific analyses and deliverables are selected in the Trial workspace. Start Trial on the Company request opens creation with that exact request selected and retains a link back to the Company. If the request already created a Trial, open that existing Trial instead of creating another request. The general Trial creation flow also supports searching and paging through available requests. Commercial and Scientific Operations independently approve a frozen scope, then a Prospect organization administrator accepts it. The CRM request review does not replace either Trial approval. See Trial Projects. Trial milestones appear on the Company and Opportunity activity history. A pending CRM publication does not block laboratory work. The Trial shows pending milestones and provides Retry CRM publication; retries preserve the original event identity. Sales updates the Opportunity stage separately from Trial scientific completion.

guides.title: Reports and administration
guides.summary: Interpret commercial reports and manage pipelines, fields, views, duplicates, imports, and exports.

sections.heading: Reports and administration
sections.text: Reports explain current commercial state. Administration controls pipelines, stages, custom fields, saved views, duplicate review, imports, and audited exports.

sections.heading: Read Reports
sections.text: Open Reports to review: open Opportunity count, USD open amount, USD weighted forecast, and win rate stage-level counts, USD values, weighted values, and average age owner workload across open Tasks, overdue Tasks, Leads, and Opportunities Lead-source qualification and conversion performance Activities recorded in the last 30 days Opportunity counts include every currency. Amount and weighted-forecast totals include USD records only and never imply conversion from another currency. Reports contain commercial relationship facts and must not be interpreted as scientific throughput, recognized accounting revenue, or laboratory capacity.

sections.heading: Configure pipelines and stages
sections.text: Open Administration. Create a pipeline for a distinct commercial process, then add ordered stages. Each stage has a name, position, category, probability, and a choice requiring transition reason. Only one active default pipeline supplies default conversion behavior. Deactivating a pipeline or stage removes it from new selections without erasing Opportunity or stage history. Before deactivation, review active Opportunities that still depend on it and move them through valid business transitions.

sections.heading: Configure custom fields
sections.text: Custom fields are additive CRM metadata for Company, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, or Task. Choose Text, Number, Date, Boolean, or Option; choose Internal or Restricted sensitivity; and decide whether the field is required. Option fields accept only configured choices. Required active fields appear as incomplete-data warnings until the matching record has a valid value. Deactivation stops active collection but preserves stored history. Do not create custom fields for samples, patient data, scientific results, credentials, or file contents.

sections.heading: Save and export views
sections.text: Company, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, and Task directories can save the current filters as a personal or shared view. Applying a saved view replaces the current supported filters. Export current view uses the same filters and creates an audited export record. Administration lists saved views and supports full audited exports for Company, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, and Task. Treat every downloaded CSV according to Phaeno's commercial-data handling rules.

sections.heading: Review possible duplicates
sections.text: Administration groups likely duplicate Companies and Contacts by the detected matching value. A warning never merges records automatically. Open every candidate, confirm that it represents the same legal entity or person, choose the authoritative record, and use the controlled merge action with a reason.

sections.heading: Import CSV data
sections.text: Select Preview CSV import, choose Company, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity, and select a CSV file. Imports support at most 5,000 rows and only these columns: Company: name, domain, phone, industry, source Contact: first_name, last_name, email, phone Job titles belong to Company relationships and are not accepted as standalone Contact import fields. Associate the imported Contact with a Company, then record the title on that relationship. Contact exports include primary_company and primary_company_title as derived reference columns. Lead: display_name, company_name, first_name, last_name, email, phone, source Opportunity: name, company_name, product_interest, amount, currency, next_step. When supplied, product_interest must be PSeqLabService or PSeqKit. Preview shows valid, duplicate, and invalid counts. Duplicate rows are skipped. Any invalid row blocks the commit so the source can be corrected as one controlled batch. An imported Opportunity's company_name must exactly match an active CRM Company; it starts in the first active stage of the default active pipeline. The batch identity is derived from record type and file facts so an unchanged retry is idempotent. Do not rename or alter a file merely to force a second commit. Tasks are excluded from import because every Task requires an explicit owning CRM record.

guides.title: Troubleshooting and recovery
guides.summary: Resolve access, duplicate, stale-update, conversion, stage, import, Task, and handoff problems safely.

sections.heading: CRM troubleshooting and recovery
sections.text: CRM preserves optimistic concurrency and consequential history. Recover by refreshing and using the owning workflow; do not repair failures with duplicate records or rewritten history.

sections.heading: CRM is unavailable
sections.text: CRM requires an active Phaeno platform-administrator account in the Phaeno organization context. If the toolbar item is absent, confirm the selected organization and your account role. If the page reports that CRM access is required, ask a platform administrator to review your authorization rather than sharing credentials or using another person's session.

sections.heading: A list is empty or will not load
sections.text: Clear search and saved-view filters, confirm active/inactive filtering, and refresh once. An empty result differs from a failed request; retain the displayed error when escalating. Do not create a replacement record until search and duplicate review confirm that the record does not exist. The Company's People, Sales, and Requests tabs show a loading message or a specific failure with Retry for the affected records. A refresh failure may leave previously loaded records visible with a warning; it does not mean the Company has no records. Retry the affected section before associating a Contact, preparing an invitation, or choosing an Opportunity for a request.

sections.heading: A record may be duplicated
sections.text: Open Administration and review the possible-duplicate group. Compare identity, domains, email, associations, activity, Tasks, Opportunities, and Portal-access status. Merge only a confirmed duplicate and record the reason. A merge is not the repair for a changed employer, renamed organization, or distinct legal entity.

sections.heading: An update is stale
sections.text: Another user changed the record after your page loaded. Reload, review the newer version and history, and re-enter only the change that is still correct. Do not repeatedly submit the stale form or ask for concurrency protection to be bypassed.

sections.heading: A Lead will not convert
sections.text: Confirm the Lead is Qualified, required Company choices are complete, the selected pipeline is active, and duplicate warnings have been resolved. If conversion may already have completed, refresh the Lead and open its recorded Company, Contact, or Opportunity results before retrying.

sections.heading: An Opportunity will not move
sections.text: Confirm the destination stage belongs to the Opportunity's pipeline and remains active. Enter a reason when the stage requires one, especially Lost or Abandoned outcomes. Reload stale Opportunities before retrying. Do not edit pipeline configuration to force one transition.

sections.heading: A Task status will not change
sections.text: Blocked requires a reason. Completed and Cancelled Tasks do not offer Update; create a new follow-up Task when more work is needed. For a recurring Task, verify whether completing it already created the next occurrence.

sections.heading: An import cannot commit
sections.text: Preview must contain no invalid rows. Correct unsupported headers, missing required values, malformed currency or amount values, unmatched Opportunity company names, and row-count limits in the source CSV, then preview again. Duplicate rows are skipped; do not modify identifying data merely to force them through. If the same file may already have committed, review the batch result and affected records. The idempotency boundary is designed to make an unchanged retry safe.

sections.heading: A Company request appears missing or repeated
sections.text: Refresh the Company workspace and open Requests to find the displayed request number. A repeated operation key is rejected as an existing handoff; inspect the original request before submitting anything new. Use the central Requests queue to follow it through Needs decision, Approved / needs work, and Completed / history. Never create a second CRM Company or change the request identity merely to make another request appear.

sections.heading: Protected or scientific information was entered
sections.text: Stop adding or copying the information. Preserve the record and contact the appropriate Phaeno privacy or security owner for controlled remediation. Do not duplicate the content in a support message, Activity, Task, export, or replacement CRM record.

guides.title: Curated catalog and publishing
guides.summary: Snapshot ready sources, validate complete packages, publish immutable versions, and retire safely.

sections.heading: Curated catalog and publishing
sections.text: A curated package is a Portal-facing, immutable version built from one exact ready source revision. Publication creates a stable package identity and manifest; it does not grant the package to an organization.

sections.heading: Create the curated draft
sections.text: Select the ready source revision and review the source identity, revision, ownership and de-identification evidence, files, checksums, and snapshot time. The draft captures that source state so later source changes cannot alter it. Add the Portal-facing title, summary, release notes, scientific context, and dataset-specific metadata required for users to understand the package. Do not copy internal investigation notes or storage keys into the visible description.

sections.heading: Validate the complete package
sections.text: Before publication, confirm: every required record and file is included; the manifest is complete and checksummed; ownership and de-identification evidence is present; every file passed managed-storage and malware checks; source lineage points to the exact ready revision; and policy and audience-eligibility requirements are satisfied. Publication is atomic. A failed validation leaves an editable draft and exposes no partial version.

sections.heading: Publish and manage eligibility
sections.text: Publishing creates an immutable version. Marking it eligible makes the version available to authorized Phaeno grant workflows; eligibility itself grants no tenant access. A later version has its own identity, review, manifest, and release notes. Existing organization grants remain pinned to their current version until explicitly upgraded.

sections.heading: Retire a version
sections.text: Retirement permanently prevents new grants while preserving existing grants, files, manifests, and download history. Confirm the affected active grants and provide a retained reason. Do not use retirement when the intent is immediate safety blocking; use quarantine instead.

guides.title: Governance and recovery
guides.summary: Quarantine unsafe content, investigate with purpose, close out incidents, and retry safely.

sections.heading: Governance and recovery
sections.text: Governance actions protect every organization using a curated package while preserving evidence, immutable versions, grants, and download history.

sections.heading: Quarantine immediately
sections.text: Use quarantine when ownership, de-identification, source safety, or published content becomes uncertain. Confirm the affected source, package versions, organizations, and active grants. Record the high-level concern category, internal investigation reason, and tenant-safe instructions. Quarantine overrides all grants derived from the affected source and immediately blocks tenant viewing and downloading. It suspends grants; it does not revoke them or delete content.

sections.heading: Investigate with purpose
sections.text: Quarantined content remains available only through the Phaeno investigation path. Every investigation view or download requires a recorded purpose. Keep internal evidence restricted and do not use the tenant download route.

sections.heading: Clear or withdraw
sections.text: Clear quarantine only after recording the investigation outcome and why the unchanged immutable version is safe. The confirmation should show which still-active grants will resume and which revoked or inactive grants will remain unavailable. If the content is confirmed unsafe, preserve the version as evidence and withdraw it from future use. Track one administrator attestation per affected organization, its due date, reminders, and completion evidence. Phaeno may record an externally received attestation, but the record must identify the organization contact, evidence source, and that it was Recorded by Phaeno.

sections.heading: Review notice delivery
sections.text: Grant notices use current active organization and department access when dispatched. A revoked or superseded grant may still require a notice. Deactivated users, memberships, and department-admin assignments are excluded. Organization-wide notices go to organization administrators. Quarantine, clearance, withdrawal, and attestation reminders continue to reach current active organization administrators for affected organizations during suspension, because instructions may apply to copies already held. This does not restore Portal or download access. If no eligible administrator remains, arrange follow-up and record any externally received attestation with its evidence source. A notice with no eligible recipients remains failed and eligible for retry under the normal retry limits. Review current administrator assignments and the applicable organization or department status before retrying. A successful delivery state records sender acceptance; confirm the recipient's response separately.

sections.heading: Recover failed operations
sections.text: Publication, grants, upgrades, revocations, quarantine, and clearance use version-aware, idempotent commands. Refresh before retrying a failed operation. Retry the existing provisioning or governance run rather than creating a duplicate grant or package version. Never clear a quarantine, restore access, or change an immutable version merely to resolve an integration or UI error.

guides.title: Organization grants
guides.summary: Grant, upgrade, and revoke exact package versions without implicit access changes.

sections.heading: Organization grants
sections.text: An organization grant gives one Prospect, Customer, or Partner organization access to one exact immutable curated-package version. Organization kind, relationship stage, eligibility, or publication never creates access automatically.

sections.heading: Create the grant
sections.text: Confirm the active target Company access scope and package identity. If access has not been approved, use Open Company access setup, create or open the CRM Company, and complete its reviewed online-access request. Return to the pending data assignment; its selected version and access scope remain in the browser session. Select a published, eligible, non-quarantined, non-retired version and review the complete package contents before confirmation. The grant operation should show: target organization and organization kind; package and exact version; current grant state and any superseded version; files and manifest included in the package; and the access consequence for active organization members. Company access approval and data assignment are separate actions. A failed grant never recreates the Company or its access scope.

sections.heading: Understand access
sections.text: An organization-wide grant is visible to authorized active members throughout that organization. A Department grant is visible only in that Department under the current role rules. Access is package-wide, not file-by-file. Downloads remain authorized at request time against membership, grant, version, package, and governance state.

sections.heading: Upgrade explicitly
sections.text: Publishing a newer version never moves an existing grant. An upgrade atomically supersedes the prior active grant with the selected new version and preserves the earlier grant, version, downloads, and audit history.

sections.heading: Revoke access
sections.text: Revocation immediately blocks future viewing and downloads but cannot recall files already downloaded. Require confirmation and a retained reason. Organization deactivation suspends access without revoking the grant; reactivation restores access only when the grant remains active and eligible. Prospect conversion preserves every existing grant and pinned version. Handle any desired package change as a separate grant, upgrade, or revocation action.

guides.title: Data provisioning
guides.summary: Manage Phaeno-owned sources, immutable packages, exact-version grants, and governance events.

sections.heading: Data provisioning
sections.text: Phaeno controls organization access and the lifecycle of Phaeno-owned source samples and curated package versions. Customer and Partner operational data is a separate access class and is never automatically reused for curated packages. Use the far-left sidebar beneath the toolbar to move among Source registry, Curated catalog, Organization grants, and Governance. The sidebar header identifies Data provisioning and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the edge tab. Choosing a section closes an unpinned sidebar.

sections.heading: Understand the lifecycle
sections.text: Register Phaeno-owned source material and its ownership and de-identification evidence. Complete the editable source revision and mark it ready. Snapshot one exact ready revision into a curated draft. Validate and publish an immutable package version. Mark the version eligible for the intended external audience when appropriate. Explicitly grant one exact version to an organization or one of its Departments. Preserve publication, grant, download, revocation, retirement, and governance history. Each step is explicit. Source readiness does not publish a package. Publication does not grant access. Eligibility does not grant access. A later version does not upgrade an existing grant.

sections.heading: Use the correct access
sections.text: Only authorized Phaeno users register sources, publish versions, manage eligibility, create or upgrade grants, revoke access, or open and resolve governance incidents. When assigning a package, choose All departments (organization-wide) or one active Department. Prospect, Customer, and Partner users can view only exact active versions granted organization-wide or to their currently selected Department. Department administrators see download history for that same scope; organization administrators retain access across Departments and are the only external users who can submit an organization-wide governance attestation. Company identity, relationship, membership, and lifecycle are managed in CRM → Companies. In Organization grants, Open Company access setup takes you there; Return to pending data assignment returns to the grant screen with its draft selections retained in this browser session. Data provisioning assigns packages to existing access scopes and does not create a separate tenant. A Prospect-to-Customer or Prospect-to-Partner conversion preserves the organization identity, memberships, grants, pinned versions, and audit history. Conversion never creates, replaces, upgrades, or revokes a curated-data grant. For a Customer using PSeq Lab Service, Company Departments & services shows derived, Department-specific readiness. Resolve account, administrator, entitlement, offering, order/sample/shipping/result-destination/instruction, and manual blockers before quote issuance or Customer commitment. Billing, terms, tax, and Finance approval remain visible but may be completed after acceptance; they must be complete before invoicing. Beginning pricing needs the active Customer, the selected Department's effective Ready PSeq service entitlement, active offering, and no operational block. Historical Portal readiness text is informational and does not authorize a transaction. Invitation access and email delivery are separate. Review the delivery state, sends, error, and expiry before retrying. A hard bounce requires revoking the invitation and issuing a new one to the corrected address; never copy or bypass an invitation token.

sections.heading: Protect the boundary
sections.text: Operational Customer or Partner files do not enter the source pool automatically. Every curated package is derived from an approved Phaeno-owned source revision. Keep storage keys, internal evidence, another organization’s grant state, and governance investigation detail out of tenant-facing content.

guides.title: Source registry
guides.summary: Register Phaeno-owned sources, managed files, evidence, and immutable ready revisions.

sections.heading: Source registry
sections.text: The source registry is the Phaeno-only intake for material approved for curation. It establishes ownership, de-identification, evidence, managed files, and revision lineage before any curated package can be created.

sections.heading: Register the source
sections.text: Create the source shell with the stable Phaeno identifier and the minimum descriptive context needed to distinguish it. Confirm that Phaeno owns or is authorized to use the material for the intended curated package. Customer and Partner operational data must not be reused merely because Phaeno processed it.

sections.heading: Build the draft revision
sections.text: Add required metadata, ownership and de-identification evidence, and approved files. Upload files through managed portal storage so the system records size, content type, checksum, scan state, and storage identity. The draft remains editable while validation is incomplete. Review every required field and file, then resolve validation or malware-scan failures before readiness.

sections.heading: Mark the revision ready
sections.text: Ready is an irreversible revision boundary. A ready revision is immutable and can be selected for a curated snapshot. Later corrections create a new source revision; they never mutate the revision already used by a package.

sections.heading: Discard or archive safely
sections.text: An authorized Phaeno user may discard only an unreferenced draft. Discard requires confirmation and a retained reason. A ready, archived, or curated-snapshot revision cannot be deleted through the normal workflow. Archive a ready source when it must no longer be used for new curated snapshots. Archiving does not alter packages or grants already derived from that source. If ownership, de-identification, or safety becomes uncertain after publication, use the Governance workflow. Do not edit the source evidence or silently replace files.

guides.title: Phaeno operations guide
guides.summary: Find each workflow, its owning workspace, reusable configuration, and the roles needed to act.

sections.heading: Phaeno operations guide
sections.text: The Phaeno organization workspace is the operating surface for first-party customer relationship management, organization administration, data provisioning, Customer and Partner order work, laboratory execution, public Website intake, commercial configuration, and integration recovery.

sections.heading: Navigate workspaces and guides
sections.text: The POMS dashboard, CRM, Lab operations, Order operations, Data provisioning, and Documentation use a shared sidebar anchored beneath the toolbar at the far-left edge of the screen. Its header identifies the current workspace and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. The sidebar is pinned by default, leaves a centered page in place when the left margin has room, and reflows the page only to prevent overlap. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the edge; keyboard and touch users open the same non-modal rail from the tab. Documentation automatically lists only the guides for the current organization, with an icon identifying each topic. CRM, Data provisioning, Order operations, and Laboratory operations expand to show an overview and detailed workflow guides. The group containing the current guide opens automatically; use its disclosure button to expand or collapse it.

sections.heading: Work in the Phaeno context
sections.text: Phaeno users enter the Phaeno organization context through their authenticated session. The user menu does not provide an act-as control for switching into Prospect, Customer, or Partner organizations. Manage those Companies and their access through CRM. Available workspaces and actions depend on your active Phaeno membership and assigned roles. Platform administration, order pricing, Finance, laboratory execution, scientific approval, and result release have separate responsibilities; a visible guide does not grant any of them. Ask a platform administrator to review missing access.

sections.heading: Protect your account
sections.text: After your first sign-in step, connect an authenticator app and confirm the code it displays. Store the one-time backup codes separately from the authenticator device. Never send an authenticator or backup code in email, chat, support notes, or an audit description. If both the authenticator and all backup codes are lost, contact an authorized Phaeno platform administrator. The administrator verifies your identity, resets the MFA enrollment, and revokes active sessions. You must connect a new authenticator before Portal access resumes. Email can initiate recovery but does not automatically bypass MFA.

sections.heading: Find platform work
sections.text: Dashboard uses the sidebar to show one Order Operations, Lab Operations, Accounts, or Web Operations panel at a time. Counts summarize the work or intake represented by each panel. CRM opens the complete first-party relationship, sales, and customer-access workspace. Its sidebar groups Companies and Contacts under Relationships; Leads and Opportunities under Sales; Tasks and Requests under Follow-up; Reports under Insights; and configuration under Administration. The Company is the canonical Customer, Partner, or Prospect record. Its workspace separates Overview, People, Sales, Departments & services, Requests, and Activity so you can focus on one kind of work at a time. Creating a Company does not grant access. Use the central Requests queue to review Needs decision, carry out Approved / needs work, and review Completed / history; use People for Company contacts, Portal identities, invitations, and reviewed access, and Departments & services for departments, readiness, services, and retention. Online-access approval creates only the internal tenant scope required for sign-in; product and service entitlements are managed separately, and approval never creates another customer record or a user. Web Operations is a Phaeno-administrator view of active public Website intake. Use Mailing List, Demo Requests, or Email delivery to select one panel at a time. Mailing List shows the newest active signups and identifies technical-brief requests; use Unsubscribe and confirm to remove a contact from that active list. Demo Requests shows the inquiry contact, organization, email, and submitted description; use Mark complete and confirm after the inquiry has been handled. Completed or unsubscribed items leave their active list immediately, but the original Website intake and action audit remain in POMS. Each panel paginates independently in groups of 10; its footer paginator appears only when the list has more than one page. These actions preserve Website intake history; create a CRM Company or Company request separately when commercial follow-up requires one. User management is the durable employee-access workspace. Invite a named Phaeno user with their intended Platform administrator and additive laboratory roles, edit accepted users and their roles, deactivate or reactivate accounts, and manage pending invitations there. Data provisioning manages source samples, curated packages, grants, and governance. Order operations contains Order intake, Trial projects, PSeq kits, Assembly, Attention, Result release, Finance, and Legacy integrations. Start each Customer Job from Order intake → New Customer order. Company request decisions remain in CRM; receipt and laboratory execution remain in Lab operations. Lab operations contains Phaeno-only work orders for receipt, accession, protocol execution, materials and equipment, libraries and batches, outsourced sequencing, exceptions, and scientific approval. Its sidebar contains operational work rather than role administration. Access requires an effective Lab role or platform-administrator bootstrap access. Order configuration maintains reusable defaults, the Service catalog, Analyses, Sample shipping, PSeq kits, Assembly, and Legacy links. File retention sets policies for future releases. Trial configuration is reached from Trial projects and owns Trial approvers and deliverable definitions. Docs opens the guide set for the current organization.

sections.heading: Recover Website email
sections.text: Within Web Operations, select Email delivery to inspect queued messages, provider acceptance, and failures. View attempts shows the retained attempt history and refreshes while open. Temporary failures retry automatically up to five attempts. Accepted by email provider confirms the provider accepted the message; it does not confirm inbox delivery. The queue summary shows queued, sending, and failed messages, the oldest queued message, and interrupted attempts. Needs attention shows failed messages and interrupted attempts awaiting recovery. An interrupted attempt may have reached the recipient; review its history before taking action. Use Pause email delivery during an investigation and enter a reason. The pause persists until a platform administrator selects Resume email delivery and records a reason. Your identity, time, and reason are retained in the change history. Public Website intake and manual recovery continue to queue messages while paused; attempts already in progress may finish. Resuming processes queued messages and eligible retries, without automatically resending messages already accepted by the provider. If the delivery setting changes during review, use Reload delivery status; keep reason. Editing and dismissal are temporarily blocked while saving or reloading. Review the refreshed state before submitting your preserved reason. The queue summary refreshes automatically; a loading error identifies counts that may be out of date. For an eligible active intake record, choose Queue resend, review the specific contact and recipient, and confirm. Resending can produce a duplicate if an interrupted attempt already sent the message. A five-minute wait and a current record are required; Refresh delivery status helps recover a changed record. Each staff request is audited. An older active Mailing List signup that requested a brief may show Queue technical brief when no delivery record exists. Its original delivery status is unknown. Review and confirm the recipient before queuing it. Unsubscribed contacts and completed demo requests are not eligible for recovery.

sections.heading: Separate safe and internal information
sections.text: Tenant timelines and messages must contain only tenant-safe reasons and actions. Internal notes, scientific investigation evidence, credentials, retry details, and other restricted facts stay in authorized Phaeno surfaces. Never place passwords, OAuth credentials, webhook secrets, connection strings, protected health information, or customer file contents in notes, audit descriptions, notification messages, or accounting memo fields.

sections.heading: Support users safely
sections.text: Confirm the selected organization, user membership, capability, record reference, and visible status before changing data. Ask the caller which action and status their own audience guide and workspace show. Phaeno Docs remains in the Phaeno audience; it does not offer an external-audience selector or impersonation. Do not ask users to share credentials or authentication tokens.

sections.heading: Search and browse guides
sections.text: Use Search documentation at the top of Docs to find a guide or a matching section. Results update after a short pause; use at least two characters. Try “scientific approval” or “Department administrator”. Choose Filters to narrow results by Topic, Workflow, or Guide type. Clear filters removes those selections. Browse by topic opens guides for a topic without requiring search words. Workflow links and Related guides at the end of an article provide other ways to find relevant instructions. Select a result title to open its matching section. Your browser’s Back action restores the search and filters. Search uses the guides for your current organization; it does not include the public Website or operational records. A guide’s instructions do not change your account permissions. If no guides match, try fewer words or clear the filters. If search is temporarily unavailable, use Try again or Browse all guides. A documentation update may require Refresh page; guide browsing remains available while the update finishes.

guides.title: Exceptions, rework, and cancellation
guides.summary: Classify exceptions, preserve rework history, and respond safely to cancellation requests.

sections.heading: Exceptions, rework, and cancellation
sections.text: Exceptions preserve unexpected scientific or operational facts without exposing internal investigation detail to a Customer. Rework and cancellation decisions must retain the original work and its history.

sections.heading: Classify the exception
sections.text: Choose Internal when the issue can be resolved without Customer action. Choose Customer action required only when Commercial should present a safe request to the Customer. Record the internal description, severity, blocking state, responsible role, and required next action. For Customer-action exceptions, add a separate safe summary that states what is needed without disclosing internal scientific hypotheses, other organizations, or confidential operational detail.

sections.heading: Resolve or rework
sections.text: A blocking open exception prevents scientific approval. A Lab Supervisor records the durable resolution, decision, and any authorized rework. Rework remains under the same Commercial order unless the approved Commercial process creates a new authorization. Do not delete a failed execution, consumed material, rejected library, or prior QC result. Link the rework to the original facts and record why it was required.

sections.heading: Handle cancellation requests
sections.text: The Customer request remains in Commercial review. For unreceived work, Lab Ops can report that cancellation is safe. Started work requires a bounded work-order or specimen-level decision based on receipt, consumption, execution, and sendout state. Do not force Lab work to cancelled merely because Commercial received a request. Return the Lab decision so Order Ops can approve, partially approve, or decline the Commercial cancellation and preserve any financial adjustment for PSeq Finance or the applicable Partner accounting handoff.

sections.heading: Recover projections
sections.text: Commercial receives only safe action counts, summaries, milestones, schedule health, and timing projections. If a projection is delayed, refresh and retry the durable event. Never copy internal exception data into Commercial tables or create a duplicate work order.

guides.title: Libraries, batches, and sequencing
guides.summary: Record named QC evidence, prepare libraries and batches, and track the frozen sendout manifest and custody.

sections.heading: Libraries, batches, and sequencing
sections.text: Library and batch records preserve the physical lineage from submitted specimen through prepared library and outsourced sequencing custody.

sections.heading: Prepare a library
sections.text: Create the physical library container before creating the library record. Link the source container, library container, submitted specimen, and completed preparation execution. POMS uses the selected library container's Phaeno barcode as the immutable library key; do not enter a second identifier. Record the library QC result and supporting values required by the approved procedure. Only a library with passed QC can enter a sequencing batch. If QC fails, preserve the failed library and use the documented rework or replacement path.

sections.heading: Build a batch
sections.text: A batch may contain libraries from different organizations and Commercial orders. Give it a human-friendly name and optional notes. POMS assigns the current External sequencing type and a date-stamped, scanner-safe batch number when the batch is created. The name helps operators recognize the run; the batch number remains the immutable identifier. Add only the required library identifiers and operational facts. Do not copy Customer names, prices, order notes, or other confidential Commercial details into the batch manifest. For scan-first entry, open Batches, select a draft batch under Scan libraries into a batch, and scan each physical library container. POMS accepts only a container linked to a QC passed library. An unknown barcode, non-library container, library in another state, or duplicate membership is rejected without changing the batch. A successful scan clears and refocuses the field for the next container. Confirm membership before starting the batch. Once started, preserve the membership history and use supported add, remove, or exception actions rather than rewriting the original manifest. Scanning proves the container identity used for entry; it does not replace the approved physical manifest and custody checks. When an authorized operator uses Start or Complete batch, POMS opens a confirmation modal with the observed start or completion time prefilled. The operator can correct the time when the bench event happened before it was entered; POMS stores the submitted value as UTC and retains the server audit timestamp. Use the Status filter above the batch list to focus on drafts, in-progress batches, or completed batches without changing which draft batches are available for scanning.

sections.heading: Create an outsourced sendout
sections.text: For outsourced NGS, enter the provider name, optional provider reference, expected completion, and any additional manifest notes. POMS freezes the current batch membership, library identifiers, and library-container barcodes in the sendout manifest. Confirm the physical contents against the batch before saving. Advance it through Shipped, Received by provider, Sequencing, and Complete only when the corresponding operational fact is known. Add custody events whenever responsibility or location changes. Record the event code, location or responsible party, and carrier or tracking reference when used by the approved procedure. An optional custody note captures additional operational facts.

sections.heading: Respect the implementation boundary
sections.text: The sendout tracks material, manifest, timing, provider status, and custody. Raw-file ingestion, pipeline orchestration, intermediate provenance, long-term storage, and final-output publication remain outside the current Lab Ops implementation.

sections.heading: Record library quality evidence
sections.text: For library QC, select Pass or Fail and record the observations and decision basis. Add named measurements with their values and units as needed. POMS retains those structured observations with the library; operators do not need to prepare JSON. The applicable method still determines the scientific acceptance criteria.

guides.title: Materials and equipment
guides.summary: Qualify lots and equipment, record consumption and use, and preserve traceability.

sections.heading: Materials and equipment
sections.text: Materials and equipment records show what was used, in what quantity, and whether it was suitable at the time of execution. They support scientific traceability; they are not purchasing or accounts-payable records.

sections.heading: Receive and qualify material lots
sections.text: Choose the lot kind first: Supplier lot uses a controlled material identity, supplier, supplier lot number, and storage location. Prepared reagent uses a controlled material identity, Phaeno lot number, storage location, and one or more source component lots. It does not use a supplier. Select existing controlled records when available. If a material, supplier, or storage location is new, choose the corresponding Create a new… option and enter its name in the focused modal. The entered name returns as the selected option in the lot form. The new reference is created with the lot, and POMS assigns an immutable key to a new material. Retired reference records are retained for history but are not available for new lots. Record the available quantity and unit. Use Expiration or retest date when applicable; this is a date-only field and the lot remains valid through the end of that date. Exact time-sensitive use-by control is not represented by this field. New lots show QC: Pending. A laboratory supervisor uses Record QC, confirms the QC date, and selects Pass QC or Fail QC in the modal. A failed outcome requires a reason. Passing QC makes the lot eligible for controlled work when its expiration or retest date, availability, and other rules are also satisfied. Failing QC keeps the lot blocked. POMS also retains the operator and server-recorded audit time. Only lots with Passed or Approved exception QC may be consumed in controlled work. An approved exception must retain the decision, reason, approver, and applicable scope. Expired, failed, quarantined, or otherwise unavailable lots remain blocked. When a prepared reagent is created, select each exact source lot and quantity. Every source lot must be QC-approved, unexpired, and available in the entered unit. POMS records the lineage and subtracts the component quantities atomically.

sections.heading: Record consumption
sections.text: Start the assigned execution before recording consumption. Select the exact lot, quantity, and compatible unit required by the protocol. The portal blocks unit mismatches and consumption above the available quantity. Consumption is a durable scientific fact. Do not reduce or delete it to make inventory appear correct. Use an approved correction, adjustment, or exception that preserves the original entry and reason.

sections.heading: Register equipment
sections.text: Enter the equipment name, then select an equipment type and location already used by the laboratory. Protocol equipment requirements also supply type choices, and active material-storage locations are available as location choices. If the required type or location is missing, choose Create a new…, enter its name in the focused modal, and use the returned selection. POMS assigns the immutable asset code when the equipment is created. Record the Last calibration date and Calibration due date when applicable. These are date-only laboratory facts; a time of day is not required. The due date cannot be before the last calibration date, and a last calibration date cannot be in the future. Equipment must be active and calibration-current at the time it is used.

sections.heading: Record equipment use
sections.text: Link the exact equipment record to the execution step or run. Confirm that its status and calibration cover the use time. If equipment becomes unavailable or overdue, stop new use, record the issue, and select another qualified item or follow the approved exception path. The accounting system may own a purchase-order reference, but supplier invoices, payment, and procurement approval remain outside Lab Ops.

guides.title: Laboratory operations
guides.summary: Fulfill kits, receive and accession specimens, execute controlled work, assemble data, and record release readiness.

sections.heading: Laboratory operations
sections.text: Use Receipt & accession in Lab operations to prepare return kits, identify arriving packages, compare registered tubes, and see authorized work awaiting specimens. Choose Open receipt to record custody, accession, and intake disposition in the linked Lab work order. Customer quote acceptance opens sample-list preparation; finalizing the exact compliant roster records the Commercial authorization and creates the linked Lab work order and shipment together. Do not create Lab work manually to repair an order. Use the far-left sidebar beneath the toolbar to move among Receipt & accession, Work, PSeq kits, Data assembly, Protocols, Materials, Equipment, and Batches. Work contains authorized scientific work after the receipt queue; PSeq kits and Data assembly contain their manufacturing workflows. The sidebar header identifies Lab operations and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the edge tab. Choosing a section closes an unpinned sidebar.

sections.heading: Understand the boundary
sections.text: Lab Ops owns return-kit preparation, physical PSeq kit fulfillment, shipment intake, specimen receipt, accession, container lineage, Data Assembly execution, controlled protocol execution, material and equipment use, libraries, cross-order batches, sequencing sendouts, exceptions, and scientific approval. Commercial owns order intake, the Customer or Partner order, quotes, approval, cancellation review, billing, and accounting source records. Work enters Lab Ops only through an immutable Commercial authorization. Lab Ops publishes safe milestones and action requests back to Commercial; it never exposes internal laboratory tables or investigation notes to a Customer.

sections.heading: Use the correct role
sections.text: Laboratory roles are additive Phaeno-only assignments: Lab Operator records receipt, accession, containers, execution, consumption, equipment use, libraries, batching, sendouts, custody, and exceptions. Lab Supervisor can perform operator work, approve material QC, and resolve exceptions. Protocol Administrator authors, approves, activates, and retires controlled protocol versions. Scientific Reviewer records scientific approval after execution and blocking-exception gates pass. Lab Operations Administrator can perform all Lab actions and assign Lab roles. Platform administrators retain bootstrap access. Only active Phaeno members can receive or use Lab roles; disabling or offboarding a user removes effective Lab access even if an assignment record remains. Assign the narrowest roles needed for a person's work. Separation of operator and reviewer is supported but is not mandatory for every service. Manage these assignments from User management. Select Edit on an active Phaeno user, then change the laboratory roles in that user’s single Roles group and save the record. The Lab operations sidebar contains operational laboratory work only.

sections.heading: Follow the work sequence
sections.text: Open the authorized work order and verify the expected specimens. Record receipt and accession; POMS assigns the authoritative barcode and creates the initial physical container. Apply the intake decision and preserve every derived-container relationship. Assign an active protocol version and record controlled execution. Capture material consumption, equipment use, library preparation, batching, and sendout custody as applicable. Resolve blocking exceptions and complete scientific review. Publish Ready for release back to Commercial. Every transition preserves prior state.
