Do not repair mistakes by deleting containers, overwriting protocol versions, replacing shipment history, or duplicating work orders.

sections.heading: Operational readiness boundary
sections.text: POMS now allocates checksummed Phaeno barcodes, renders Code 39 container labels, records reasoned print and failure history, supports scan-first container lookup, and adds eligible libraries to a draft batch by scan. These software controls do not prove that a particular printer, stock, scanner, browser, or environment is fit for production. This guide explains the portal workflow; it is not a laboratory SOP or evidence that a production process has been validated. Before production use, Phaeno must approve the actual minimum fields, labels, printers, scanners, reprint and degraded-mode procedures, external NGS provider identifiers and manifest/status exchange, and operational ownership. Use only approved procedures and configuration for real work.

guides.title: Service workflows, protocol control, and execution
guides.summary: Arrange approved protocols in a service workflow, assign named operators, and preserve controlled execution evidence.
taskKeywords: Service workflows, protocol control, and execution

sections.heading: Service workflows, protocol control, and execution
sections.text: Lab Ops uses a controlled service workflow to arrange reusable, versioned protocols into the approved production process. Every laboratory job and execution retains the exact workflow, stage, and protocol versions that governed it.

sections.heading: Build the service workflow
sections.text: In Lab operations → Protocols, create one Controlled service workflow for each active marketed laboratory service. POMS takes the service identity from the active Commercial catalog; do not type or maintain a separate product key. Choose Add version to open the workflow builder. Arrange stages in operating order and select the exact Approved protocol version for each stage. Mark each stage Required, Optional, or Conditional. A Conditional stage requires a plain-language condition. Add handoff criteria when the next stage depends on recorded evidence or a specific state. Save the Draft, review it, and approve it. Promote to production makes the complete workflow available for new laboratory jobs using the exact Approved protocol versions selected in its stages. The previous Production workflow becomes Retired; existing jobs remain pinned to their original workflow and protocol versions. A service has only one Production workflow at a time.

sections.heading: Control protocol versions
sections.text: A Protocol Administrator creates the protocol by entering its name and optional description, then continues directly to the structured definition builder. POMS derives a readable, immutable protocol key from the name and adds a suffix if that key is already in use. The key remains available in Edit name and description before approval when it is useful for support or integration matching, but the working list does not repeat it as user-facing protocol information. Open the protocol's labeled Actions menu. Choose Edit protocol to change the Draft's ordered steps, captures, resources, or QC gates. Edit name and description is available only until the first approval; after approval, create a new protocol identity if the name no longer represents the controlled method. The system-assigned key never changes. An identity without a saved definition is labeled Setup incomplete. Choose Edit protocol to build its initial Draft; the interface does not present this first definition as a new version. After a version is Approved, choose Create new version. The initial definition starts blank and offers an optional library-preparation example. A later version starts with the Approved definition. Build the procedure in execution order and use Add step, the move controls, duplicate, and remove actions to maintain that order. Replace example or copied content with the intended laboratory procedure before saving. For each step, enter a name and operator instructions, then choose whether the step is required, optional, or conditional. Conditional steps require a plain-language condition. Record whether the step may repeat, whether explicit operator confirmation is required, and whether a particular laboratory role is required. Add captured values only when the approved procedure requires them. Captures may be numbers, text, dates, choices, file references, or barcodes. Number captures may identify a unit, and choice captures require their permitted choices. Input materials, prepared outputs, and equipment types may be entered as comma- or line-separated requirements. A QC gate records explicit Pass, Fail, or Hold outcomes and requires acceptance criteria. Use the collapsed JSON preview only to review or copy the portable representation; do not author protocol JSON directly. Create protocol draft validates the complete definition and reserves the next version number. Cancelling after edits warns before discarding the unsaved definition. Each protocol can have only one Draft. While a Draft exists, Edit protocol replaces Create new version. Saving returns to the Protocols list, where the state is shown as Draft vN and the Actions menu exposes Review and approve. Approval is a formal, irreversible controlled release. Review and approve shows the exact ordered definition, requires an explicit attestation, requires an independent Protocol Administrator who did not author the version, and records that approver and timestamp. Approval locks the version and makes it the Approved version for future use. If another version was previously Approved, it becomes Superseded; work and service workflows already pinned to it remain unchanged. A Draft may be discarded and remains in version history as Discarded. A protocol that has never been approved may instead be permanently deleted, together with its Draft and Discarded versions, after destructive confirmation. Once any version has been approved, the protocol and its complete version history cannot be deleted. Approved, Superseded, and Discarded versions remain immutable and available to explain protocol history.

sections.heading: Assign work
sections.text: Choose Assign protocol on a laboratory job. POMS offers only stages from that job's pinned service workflow. For a specimen-scoped assignment, complete the earlier Required stages for that same specimen before assigning a later stage; work-order-scoped stages are checked against work-order-scoped executions. Optional and Conditional stages remain explicit choices. Confirm that required inputs exist and that the assigned operator has an effective Lab role. The assignment pins both the workflow stage and its exact protocol version even after a newer workflow enters Production.

sections.heading: Record execution
sections.text: On the laboratory job's Execution tab, open the execution link. The dedicated workspace shows its pinned protocol version, specimen, instructions, resource requirements, saved evidence, and remaining completion blockers. Choose Start execution before recording work. Choose Record for the next step. Enter the measurements, dates, approved choices, file references, and barcodes required by the procedure. Units appear beside the relevant capture. A file reference records an identifier; it does not upload a file. Confirm performed work when the procedure requires it. POMS checks the saved values against the pinned definition and records your identity and the time. Use Material and Equipment on the job to record consumed lots and quantities, output-container references, and equipment use. Before confirming a step's resources, check the listed inputs, outputs, and equipment against that traceability. Resource descriptions and QC acceptance criteria are controlled instructions assessed by the operator; POMS does not infer scientific thresholds or match free-text resource descriptions automatically. Record every optional and conditional step explicitly. An allowed Skip with reason requires the reason or condition assessment. Required steps cannot be skipped, and previously performed work cannot be changed into a skip. A step with a specified Lab role must be recorded by a user with that effective role. Earlier steps must be resolved before later evidence is recorded. For a QC gate, deliberately choose Pass, Fail, or Hold. Fail and Hold require a reason. They remain visible as saved evidence, mark the execution Blocked, and prevent later steps and completion until resolved through an allowed repeat or correction. Saved progress remains available when you leave and return. When all steps and QC gates are satisfied, choose Complete execution, add an optional deviation note, and confirm completion. POMS rechecks the persisted evidence and locks the completed execution. A held or finished laboratory job cannot accept new execution evidence.

sections.heading: Recover safely
sections.text: Do not edit an Approved definition to repair an execution. If a protocol is wrong, create and approve a new version; update and approve the service workflow separately when its stage composition must change. If execution data is wrong, use the supported correction or repeat-work path while preserving the original record and reason. Repeat is available only when the pinned procedure allows it. Correct repairs a data-entry error and requires a Supervisor who also has the step's required role. Both require a reason, fresh confirmations, and a new saved record. Expand Step history to review every earlier value, QC outcome, reason, operator, and timestamp. If an earlier step changes, later evidence must be reviewed and recorded again before completion. If another user changes the execution during a save, POMS reloads the current record and preserves your entered values. Review the latest history before saving again. If the original action is no longer available, close the form and use an allowed repeat or correction. Abandon execution requires a reason, stops the execution, and retains its evidence. Arrange a new execution for replacement work. Historical unstructured definitions or results remain preserved with a recovery message; a Protocol Administrator must prepare a valid new approved version for new work. POMS does not silently rewrite controlled history.

sections.heading: Assign an operator
sections.text: When assigning a protocol stage, choose an active laboratory operator, supervisor, or operations administrator by name. Assignment is optional; POMS retains the selected person with the execution. Select the specimen before choosing its eligible workflow stage so earlier required work is checked in the correct specimen scope.

guides.title: Receipt and accession
guides.summary: Match a packet and registered tube, continue to explicit receipt and accession, and preserve container lineage.

sections.heading: Receipt and accession
sections.text: Receipt and accession connect the Customer’s submitted specimen identity to the physical material handled in the laboratory. Record these steps in sequence and never create an unlinked laboratory specimen.

sections.heading: Record receipt
sections.text: Open the authorized Lab work order and confirm the expected submitted specimen, service, and Customer-safe identifiers. Record when and where the physical item arrived and any intake observation permitted by the approved procedure. Receipt does not accept the specimen for processing. It establishes custody and allows accession to begin. If the physical item cannot be matched safely to the expected specimen, stop and record an exception rather than guessing. When an incoming package includes a Phaeno shipment packet, open Lab operations > Receipt & accession and scan the packet and each registered supplier tube first. That comparison identifies the exact expected sample and linked Lab work but does not record receipt. After a tube matches, choose Continue to receipt and accession. POMS carries the packet and tube into the work order, checks them again, and shows the matched Customer sample. Record receipt, then confirm accession in the next dialog. The known sample label, tube quantity and unit, packet, tube barcode, and recorded location are carried forward for review. The packet barcode is not a specimen or container barcode and must not be copied into an accession or container field.

sections.heading: Accession the specimen
sections.text: Accession only after receipt. Choose a unique accession number, then record location, quantity and unit when tracked, and an optional retention date. For a shipment with a frozen registered-tube crosswalk, scan both the packet and each matched tube during accession. POMS validates the exact shipment, specimen, and tube-slot association and adopts every qualified permanent supplier barcode as a submitted-container identity. Multiple submitted tubes for one sample use the same specimen accession and create separate containers linked to that specimen. POMS does not create or print a second label for those tubes. For every other submitted specimen, POMS assigns its own authoritative barcode as before. The label window renders the current container identity as a Code 39 barcode through the browser and installed printer driver. Enter the reason, open the system print dialog, and inspect the physical label before choosing Label printed. POMS increments the print count only after that confirmation. If the label did not print correctly, enter the failure details and choose Record failed attempt; the failure remains in history without falsely counting a usable label. Every POMS-generated label reprint requires a reason and renders the same current container identity. A reprint or failed attempt adds a separate history event; it does not replace the barcode or erase an earlier print. Registered supplier tubes have no POMS print action. Verify readable text, barcode, accession, container, and adhesion using the approved bench procedure before processing continues.

sections.heading: Scan and locate a container
sections.text: Use Work > Scan a container to find the exact work order, accession, container status, location, parent barcode, and associated library. Place the cursor in the container-barcode field and scan either an adopted registered supplier barcode or a POMS-generated barcode. Code 39 start and stop characters and letter case are normalized; an altered checksum, incomplete barcode, or unknown barcode is rejected without opening another record. The field returns focus after the result so repeated scans remain efficient.

sections.heading: Preserve physical lineage
sections.text: Create child containers for aliquots, prepared reagents, libraries, or other derived materials. Select the immediate parent container and record the quantity and unit required by the approved procedure. POMS assigns each child container its own barcode and opens its label window after creation. The lineage must allow an operator to scan a derived container and trace it through its immediate parent to the submitted specimen. Do not reuse a barcode, move material by editing its parent, or delete a container to repair history. Record the supported correction or new derived container.

sections.heading: Apply the intake decision
sections.text: After accession, record Accepted, On hold, or Rejected. Holds and rejections require an approved reason code and a safe explanation when Customer action is required. When every expected specimen has an intake decision, the work order reaches Received.

guides.title: Scientific approval and release readiness
guides.summary: Select the complete output package, record independent scientific approval, and hand publication to a Result Release Manager.

sections.heading: Scientific approval and release readiness
sections.text: Scientific approval is the final Lab Ops decision. It confirms that the authorized laboratory work satisfied the configured execution and exception gates. It is not a Customer file publication action.

sections.heading: Enter scientific review
sections.text: Move work into Scientific review only after required receipt, accession, executions, QC, libraries, batches, and sendout facts are complete for the approved release scope. Confirm that every assigned execution is completed or explicitly abandoned, every blocking exception is resolved, and the registered final-result package has every expected checksummed, malware-clean artifact. The Scientific Reviewer should be able to trace the submitted specimen through containers, material lots, equipment, protocol versions, captured results, library preparation, batches, and provider custody as applicable.

sections.heading: Record the approval
sections.text: Choose Record scientific approval, then select the complete output package by Customer sample, version, and file count. Review its file names and manifest checksum. POMS uses the service workflow for the release definition and records the reviewer and approval time. Enter an optional Customer-visible QC summary using ordinary text. Approval pins that immutable package; it does not upload or alter artifacts. If several sample packages are ready, approve each package separately. Previously approved packages remain pinned while later packages undergo their own review. When no complete, checksummed, malware-clean package is available, the approval action remains blocked. The reviewer must be different from every actor who recorded receipt, accessioning, execution, QC, library, batch, or sendout work in scope. A protocol author cannot approve or activate that protocol version. If either actor-separation or scientific gates fail, leave the work in review and create the appropriate exception or rework action.

sections.heading: Publish readiness
sections.text: Approval moves the Lab work order to Ready for release and publishes the controlled Customer-safe milestone to Commercial. Commercial may receive the milestone, schedule health, expected timing, and safe QC projection defined by the contract.

sections.heading: Respect the release boundary
sections.text: Ready for release automatically creates the Commercial release candidate for the approved package. It does not publish the result. A Result Release Manager still controls Customer visibility, and payment/credit facts never gate PSeq release. If the Lab-to-Commercial event fails, retry the existing durable projection. Do not duplicate the approval, recreate the work order, or manually mark the Customer file released.

sections.heading: Review the Customer release
sections.text: A Result Release Manager opens Order operations > Result release, chooses the recognizable job and sample, and reviews the package detail before confirming publication. The detail joins scientific approval, file evidence, and release state. File administrators also see the retention receipt and preservation controls there; those permissions do not grant release authority.

guides.title: PSeq billing, cash, and result release
guides.summary: Review PSeq invoices, attach receipt evidence, preview imports, allocate and reconcile cash, and release scientifically approved results.
taskKeywords: PSeq billing, cash, and result release

sections.heading: PSeq billing, cash, and result release
sections.text: POMS owns operational accounts receivable for PSeq Lab Service. Result release is scientifically governed and never gated by payment balance or credit. Partner PSeq Kit and Partner data-assembly payment/release rules remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Find the Finance record
sections.text: Finance actions depend on your assigned responsibility: Billing Operators maintain billing and invoice adjustments, Cash Operators record and allocate receipts and submit reconciliations, and Cash Reconcilers independently approve reconciliations. Result Release Manager and file-administration authority remain separate. Open Order Ops → Finance. Choose Invoices and aging, Receipts, Customer billing, Import receipts, or Reconciliation. Open a record by its invoice, receipt, Customer or reconciliation number. The detail shows its current state and permitted actions. Return to Finance to keep the previous Customer filter and section. The Customer filter narrows the displayed records; aging summarizes all Customers, and Export all invoices and Export all receipts include all Customers.

sections.heading: Configure and issue PSeq documents
sections.text: Record billing contact/address and Net 30 terms by default. Record Taxable, Exempt, or NonTaxable, including the approved rate or exemption evidence. Finance approval is required before the tax determination can be used. If the profile is complete and approved at quote issuance, POMS includes calculated tax and freezes billing, tax, terms, currency, and configuration version in the quote. Zero calculated tax is valid. If the profile is not ready, issue an explicitly pre-tax quote. Complete and approve the profile before invoicing; POMS then calculates tax and freezes the current billing terms in the invoice. Job completion idempotently creates one numbered invoice and immutable PDF. Due date is completion plus the applicable snapshotted terms. POMS calculates the approved tax rate without a tax engine. Never edit an issued invoice; use an append-only credit, debit, or write-off adjustment.

sections.heading: Release PSeq results
sections.text: Open Order Ops → Result release, then open the package identified by its Customer, Job and sample. The detail connects scientific review, manifest, release, retention and receipt. A Customer result may be published only when the specific sample package is complete, checksummed, malware-clean, and scientifically approved. The Result Release Manager releases or withdraws a version. Other samples may remain in progress. Do not consult invoice balance or credit status for this decision. Corrections create a new package, scientific approval, and release version. Preserve notification, Customer download, retention warning/cutoff/grace/deletion, withdrawal, and authorized reissue evidence.

sections.heading: Review governed result retention
sections.text: New PSeq releases use the effective versioned policy from File retention, including an active Organization override. The package and laboratory release share the same first release instant and freeze their policy and deadlines together. Existing schedules keep their original dates; do not change them by editing current configuration. The Customer package shows full-response download completion and the frozen standard/final dates. Grace remains usable when any artifact was undownloaded at the standard deadline; later completion does not shorten grace. New download requests close at the applicable deadline even if cleanup has not run. A request-only historical download event is not completion evidence. Success saved after the standard deadline cannot cancel grace. If download timing cannot be verified, ask technical support to recover the retained timing evidence; do not recreate the release or change its dates. This timing-recovery error is separate from the Retention notices queue. Where governed retention processing is enabled, POMS queues one warning for an incomplete package and one grace notice if grace applies. A delayed warning is skipped once all files have completed or the standard deadline has passed. Queued notices use current active Organization admins; they contain the package reference, deadline, and an authenticated Portal link. Use Owned attention queues → Retention notices to find urgent missing-recipient or delivery failures. Review the organization and administrator access, correct delivery configuration when needed, then retry the existing record in the notification workspace. Recreating a release or notification is not a recovery step. A failure can reopen the Operations item until the underlying notice is recovered. Deadlines remain unchanged. Physical cleanup remains separately controlled. A closed download window is not proof of byte deletion, and a queued message is not proof of receipt. Access withdrawal or deactivation stops a governed transfer; restoring access does not resume that transfer.

sections.heading: Record and reconcile cash
sections.text: In Receipts, choose Record receipt. Enter Customer, payer, amount, received date, payment method, bank reference and external reference. Attach evidence as PDF, PNG, JPEG or text, up to 10 MB. The file must pass the configured scanner before the receipt is recorded; an unavailable scanner leaves the receipt unsaved and preserves your entries. An optional note adds context. Open a saved receipt to download its evidence, allocate it to a same-Customer invoice, or reverse it when no allocation remains. In Import receipts, select Customer and source, then choose a CSV file or paste its contents. Required headers are source, external_id, date, amount, currency, payer, reference and memo. Preview import validates the file. Review the frozen Customer, source, rows and total, then confirm. Only the operator who reviewed that preview can confirm it. If another operator already owns the file review, ask them to complete it; do not change the file identity to bypass that ownership. If the Customer, totals, or saved version changed, review a fresh preview before confirmation. Change input returns to editing and requires a fresh preview. An earlier response cannot replace a preview for changed input. Repeating your unconfirmed preview resumes the same batch; confirmed files cannot be imported twice. Imports create unapplied receipts and retain their source evidence. Matching suggestions never apply cash. Allocate explicitly so partial, one-receipt/many-invoice, many-receipt/one-invoice, overpayment, and unapplied cash remain visible. Reversals retain actor and reason. A Cash Operator submits a balanced reconciliation; a different Cash Reconciler who contributed none of its activity approves the immutable closeout report.

sections.heading: Apply Partner assembly release gates
sections.text: An approved output release must reference the accepted input revision and active assembly profile. Its accounting source record is created at output approval. A Partner with approved assembly credit may receive the output under its terms; otherwise the files remain on payment hold until a separately approved payment-confirmation workflow exists.

sections.heading: Diagnose a blocked release
sections.text: Review package completeness, checksum/scan state, scientific approval, release decision, notification, and retention independently from invoice/receipt/allocation/reconciliation. Never bypass a failed package gate by attaching a file manually or changing an unrelated workflow status. Use the owned attention queues for overdue invoices, unapplied cash, and reconciliation differences.

sections.heading: Support general Lab and Assembly downloads
sections.text: Where general retention enforcement is enabled, individual files and whole ZIPs use the release's frozen policy and verified completion. A closed window prevents new requests, while an admitted transfer can finish within its time limit. Current file withdrawal, scan failure, Organization/Department access removal, or release withdrawal stops active downloads. A failed ZIP does not count its files from that attempt. Partner payment-release rules still apply. Recover missing timing evidence through technical support without recreating the release or changing dates. General download enforcement does not itself schedule warning/grace emails or activate storage cleanup. Preserve the original contract for undated historical releases. Where general Lab/Assembly retention processing is enabled, the same warning, grace, and Retention notices recovery workflow applies to those releases. The Lab notice opens the laboratory job; the Assembly notice opens its assembly request. Recipients are current active Organization admins, including admins appointed after the notice was queued. Department-only members and notification routing aliases are not recipients. Retry the existing failed notification after correcting the cause, then review the Operations item. Preserve the original release and dates. General and governed PSeq notice processing are activated separately; a disabled process does not create or dispatch its scheduled notices. Released package schedules link to retained receipts. Receipts preserve file manifests, checksums, deadline/completion/deletion facts and reissue lineage after byte deletion. For preservation, quarantine, or linking a newly approved reissue, use Configuration and recovery.

guides.title: Customer lab authorization
guides.summary: Start a Customer Job for its Department, resolve readiness by stage, issue pricing, and authorize Lab work after sample finalization.

sections.heading: Customer lab authorization
sections.text: Customer laboratory work enters Order Ops as a Commercial request. Order Ops validates the Job-level specimen count, biological-source composition, storage, safety, and service profile before pricing. Individual samples do not exist yet.

sections.heading: Initiate an order for a Customer
sections.text: An authorized Phaeno order-pricing user can begin the pricing profile when the Customer is already known and does not need to create the request first. Open Order operations, select Order intake, and choose New Customer order. Search by Company name and select the active Customer, then choose the Department that owns the Job. Customers remain visible even when setup is incomplete. Review Before starting pricing, Before issuing a quote, and Before invoicing for that Department. Starting pricing requires the active Customer, an effective Ready PSeq Lab Service entitlement, the active specimen offering, and no operational block. It does not require an online administrator yet. Follow the setup links for unmet requirements, then return to the same order draft. Enter a unique Job name, every biological source and sample count, the shared storage requirements and safety declaration, and any Customer-safe Job notes. If Sales discussed a price, select Propose a price, enter the proposed USD price per specimen, and optionally add Customer-safe pricing context. A proposal is not a quote and does not authorize work. Do not enter individual sample IDs, tube barcodes, patient identifiers, or PHI. Confirm that the pricing details contain no patient identifiers, PHI, or unnecessary personal data, then select Start pricing. POMS creates the Customer-owned Job with one immutable submitted request revision and opens it in Quote in preparation. Review the committed sample count, source composition, storage, and safety facts on the operational detail. If a price was proposed, select Review proposed price and compare the proposal, active catalog price, difference, and calculated subtotal. Approve it unchanged or amend the unit price; an amendment requires an internal reason. Before issuing the quote, complete every non-billing readiness blocker, including activating a Customer administrator who can receive and approve it. Billing readiness may be completed after acceptance but is required before invoicing. The editor preselects the required PSeq Lab Service, explains that it is priced per specimen, and sets its read-only quantity from the Job's committed specimen count. The required line cannot be removed. Additional active catalog lines may be added with a per-unit price and a quantity chosen for that quote. Permanent accounting codes remain available in Order configuration but are not shown as quote-entry guidance. If the designated item is missing, inactive, or not priced per specimen, quote issuance is paused until Order configuration is corrected. POMS validates the item identity, unit, and committed quantity again on the server. POMS sends no Customer notice while a Phaeno-initiated Job remains Quote in preparation. Issuing or revising the quote rechecks ordering eligibility and the approver list, makes the quote available immediately, moves the Job to Quote issued, and notifies every active Customer administrator. The Customer can approve it; Phaeno cannot approve on the Customer's behalf. The accepting administrator becomes the Job's acting Customer contact for ordinary later notices. High-impact events, including cancellation by Phaeno and result release, continue to notify all active Customer administrators.

sections.heading: Review the request
sections.text: Confirm that the Customer has an active laboratory-service entitlement and that the selected service is currently offered. Review the requested specimen count, each source group and count, shared handling and safety declarations, and Customer notes. Request a targeted correction when information is incomplete or unsafe rather than rewriting Customer data internally. Keep internal review notes separate from the reason shown to the Customer. The initial workflow is not a PHI intake path; do not ask for or store patient-identifying information.

sections.heading: Issue and accept the quote
sections.text: The Customer or Sales price proposal is part of the submitted request revision, not a quote. POMS preserves its unit price, note, proposer, and time. The issued quote records whether Phaeno approved that proposal or amended it, along with the responsible Commercial reviewer and decision time. When dual control is enabled, a Phaeno proposer cannot review the same proposal. The quote is a versioned, immutable Commercial offer for one job. Confirm the configured service, quantities, prices, currency, expected turnaround information, and expiration before issuance. Tax is calculated by POMS: when the complete billing and tax profile is Finance-approved, the quote includes and freezes tax; otherwise the quote is explicitly pre-tax and tax is calculated from the approved profile at invoicing. Saving the issued POMS quote makes it available for Customer acceptance. Cancel, Close, or Escape asks you to keep editing or discard unsaved quote changes. Dismissal is unavailable while the quote is being issued or its current record is being refreshed. A stale-record response preserves your entries; review the refreshed Job and pricing before deliberately submitting again. Customer acceptance performs one Commercial operation that: records the accepted quote revision and frozen pricing profile; and opens post-acceptance sample-list preparation. After the Customer enters or imports the exact compliant sample list, finalization atomically creates the immutable laboratory work authorization, linked Lab work order, shipment, and physical tube slots. Do not create a Lab work order manually if finalization fails. Resolve the reported roster or shipping-configuration issue and retry the durable operation. Physical samples must not arrive before quote acceptance and exact roster finalization create the authorized shipment. Quarantine and escalate an unexpected package under the approved receiving and custody exception. Do not accession, process, bill, or attach it to executable Job work.

sections.heading: Respect the Lab boundary
sections.text: After acceptance, Order Ops continues to own Customer communication, Commercial holds, cancellation review, billing, files, and publication. Open the linked work from the order or from Lab operations > Receipt & accession. Lab Ops owns return-kit preparation, shipment identification, receipt, accession, physical lineage, controlled execution, exceptions, and scientific approval. The Lab milestone Ready for release means the scientific gate passed. It does not upload, scan, attach, or publish a result. PSeq result publication still requires the governed file and release checks. PSeq scientific result release is independent of invoice balance, credit status, and payment; Partner workflows retain their separate commercial rules.

guides.title: Data assembly
guides.summary: Coordinate commercial quotes and decisions with Lab-owned input validation, processing, QC, and output approval.

sections.heading: Partner data assembly
sections.text: Order Ops owns the Commercial Data Assembly order, quote, approval, cancellation, and accounting source record. Lab Ops owns input validation, processing milestones, quality review, and immutable output release. Inputs and outputs are manufacturing records; they are not source samples for Data Provisioning. Find the Commercial order in Order operations > Assembly. Open Lab operations > Data assembly to validate the submitted input and perform the manufacturing workflow. When Lab accepts the input, Commercial staff issue the quote from the linked order; manufacturing continues after Partner acceptance.

sections.heading: Validate the submission
sections.text: Confirm the active Partner, project reference, purchase-order requirement, selected active assembly profile, required metadata, and uploaded input revision. Validate file type, size, completeness, malware-scan state, and every profile-specific requirement. When the submission cannot pass input validation, Lab staff place the manufacturing record on hold and document the issue. Commercial staff use the linked order to request a targeted Partner correction or reject work that is unsafe, unsupported, or outside the offered profile. A correction creates a new input revision; it must not rewrite the revision that was reviewed previously.

sections.heading: Quote and accept the job
sections.text: Prepare the per-job quote from the current assembly offering and preserve its profile, price, currency, and expiration snapshot. Issuing the POMS quote makes it available to the Partner immediately. Acceptance records the immutable Commercial commitment and queues the work.

sections.heading: Process and review
sections.text: Record processing milestones against the accepted input revision and selected profile. Internal implementation details and intermediate files remain internal. When processing is complete, perform the configured quality review and document any hold or required correction. Open Review outputs to inspect every uploaded output and its scan state, including files uploaded in an earlier session. POMS builds the output manifest from the uploaded files and pinned processing run; operators do not type a manifest or repeat the pipeline provenance.

sections.heading: Approve an output release
sections.text: An output release is immutable and identifies: the exact source input revision; the assembly profile and version; the output manifest and included files; checksums, scan state, and generation time; and the quality-review and approval facts. Approve a new release rather than replacing a prior release. POMS creates the accounting source record, then applies the Partner’s assembly-credit gate. Credit-approved work can be released under Net 30; work without approved credit remains on payment hold because manual payment confirmation is not yet implemented.

guides.title: Holds, cancellations, and adjustments
guides.summary: Pause work safely, decide cancellation requests, preserve completed work, and account for adjustments.

sections.heading: Holds, cancellations, and adjustments
sections.text: Holds and cancellation decisions preserve work already performed. They do not erase shipments, Lab execution, input revisions, output releases, Commercial documents, or audit history.

sections.heading: Place and release holds
sections.text: Phaeno may place an active workflow on hold for an operational, Commercial, validation, shipping, or Customer-action reason. Record a concise tenant-safe explanation and separate internal notes. A hold pauses the affected next action; it does not silently change quote, payment, scientific, or release state. Release a hold only after the blocking condition is resolved. The release is an audited Phaeno action and should reference the corrected fact or approved exception.

sections.heading: Handle cancellation timing
sections.text: A draft or other unaccepted commitment may be withdrawn under its workflow rules. After quote acceptance or reagent-order acceptance, cancellation becomes a request for Phaeno review. Decide the request as approved, partially approved, or declined based on work performed, material committed, quantities shipped, and outputs already released. For Customer laboratory work, Order Ops asks Lab Ops whether unreceived work can be cancelled before committing the Commercial decision. Started or specimen-level work requires a bounded manual decision; do not force Lab into a cancelled state.

sections.heading: Preserve unaffected work
sections.text: A partial cancellation can retain completed samples, shipped reagent quantities, or accepted assembly work while removing only the approved remainder. Preserve prior revisions, manifests, packing slips, releases, and Customer-visible history.

sections.heading: Record Commercial adjustments
sections.text: Record the portal cancellation decision without editing the original Commercial snapshot. For PSeq Customer Jobs, Finance records the applicable credit, debit, or write-off in Order operations → Finance; issued invoices and accepted quotes retain their original snapshots. Partner workflows retain their manual accounting handoff using the stable commercial source references. Reconcile the correction in the workflow that owns the original document.

guides.title: Integration failures and recovery
guides.summary: Recover original invitations and notices, inspect failed projections, and recognize unavailable historical connectors.

sections.heading: Accounting and notification recovery
sections.text: A failed notice or integration remains attached to the original business record with its attempts and error history. Use Company People for invitation access and delivery recovery, Attention for operational follow-up, and the owning Lab, Trial, or release record for scientific publication. Native PSeq accounts receivable is maintained in Finance; retained accounting connectors serve historical or non-PSeq work.

sections.heading: Triage the failure
sections.text: Open Attention for the owned cross-workflow exception or Legacy integrations for a retained connector/notification event. Identify the affected record, current delivery state, owner, age, attempts, next action, and tenant-visible consequence. Determine whether the local operation committed successfully before taking recovery action. Common states include: Invitation queued/failed/bounced/needs attention while access remains separately pending, accepted, expired, or revoked; Projection or scan failed while the immutable result package remains unreleased; failed notification delivery after the underlying portal action already succeeded.

sections.heading: Retry safely
sections.text: Refresh the workflow before investigating a missing accounting row. Do not recreate the order, quote, shipment, output approval, or result completion to force another row. Use the stable source ID when reconciling repeated report downloads. If an invitation hard-bounced, revoke and reissue to a corrected address rather than retrying it. If a result or delivery already exists, inspect that original record instead of creating another package or delivery. If a notification failed, retry it without repeating the underlying business transition. If QuickBooks is not configured, catalog, document, or payment recovery reports the connector as unavailable and records Needs attention. It does not create an invoice, payment, or successful zero balance. Preserve the existing record and ask the responsible administrator to resolve the connector; repeating the request cannot configure it. Maintain the active Service catalog directly in Order configuration → Service catalog. Partner Assembly credit settings remain applicable to their own workflow.

sections.heading: Communicate the boundary
sections.text: Keep operational state, accounting-source readiness, credit, file release, and notification delivery separate. An accounting question does not undo an issued quote or scientific completion. A failed email does not reverse the order action recorded in the portal. Escalate only after the operational record, report range, stable entry ID, and notification history have been reviewed. Include safe identifiers; never include credentials, payment data, or customer-confidential scientific detail in support notes.

guides.title: Order operations
guides.summary: Start each Customer order in Intake, manage commercial decisions, and continue Lab, Finance, and release work in their owning screens.

sections.heading: Order operations
sections.text: Order operations is the Commercial workspace for Customer laboratory orders, Partner PSeq kit orders, and Partner data assembly requests. Use it for each order's pricing, commercial decisions, follow-up, Finance, and result publication. Reusable defaults and scientific offerings are maintained in Order configuration. When starting a Customer Job, select its Company and Department. A single available Department is selected automatically. The Department owns the Job and determines Customer access and the applicable service rule; a Blocked Department rule cannot be bypassed by a Ready organization default. Use the far-left sidebar beneath the toolbar to move among Order intake, Trial projects, PSeq kits, Assembly, Attention, Result release, Finance, and Legacy integrations, subject to your explicit roles. Order intake is the single entry point for paid Customer orders, sales handoffs, commercial review, pricing, and quotes. Trial projects handles no-charge evaluations. Choose New Customer order in Order intake. Select the Customer and Department, then review Customer readiness. Active Customers remain selectable even when their setup is incomplete. Requirements under Before starting pricing must be resolved first. Expand Later requirements for additional quote and invoice setup; those items do not block creating the order for pricing. Retry a failed readiness check without discarding your entries. Enter the Job name, sample counts by biological source, shared storage requirements, and safety declaration. You may also record a proposed price and optional notes. Start pricing saves the order and opens its detail workspace. An active Customer administrator is required before quote issuance. Exact sample IDs and tube counts are entered after quote acceptance; sample-list finalization authorizes the laboratory and shipping workflow. Billing setup may be completed after acceptance, before invoicing. Order intake owns this per-order process; reusable setup is maintained in Order configuration and the Company workspace. The sidebar header identifies Order operations and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the edge tab. Choosing a section closes an unpinned sidebar.

sections.heading: Enter and find orders
sections.text: Order intake covers Customer and Partner commercial requests through review, pricing, quote issuance, and Customer acceptance. Held orders remain in active intake. Use On hold to focus on blockers and All orders and history to find accepted, completed or cancelled work. Laboratory execution continues in Lab Ops. PSeq kits shows commercial status and opens the same order in Lab Ops for review, substitutions, backorders, shipments and fulfillment. Assembly shows commercial context and opens the same request in Lab Ops for processing, quality review and output release. Attention owns invitation, readiness, staged-order, projection/scan, unreleased-result, overdue-invoice, unapplied-cash, and reconciliation-difference exceptions. Result release publishes a scientifically approved, complete PSeq package per sample without a payment gate. Finance owns PSeq invoices, receipts/import, explicit allocation, aging, and reconciliation. Legacy integrations covers retained accounting-connector and notification recovery outside the active native PSeq AR workflow. Search Order intake by order, Job, Company, or request number. Order search runs across all matching records, with 25 orders per page. Pending CRM handoffs appear on the first active-intake page. The view, search and page stay in the address so you can return to the same queue. Clear filters restores active intake. A PSeq Lab Service row identifies an optional proposed price so Commercial users can find pricing decisions without opening every record. On the order, Review proposed price compares the proposed USD price per specimen with the active catalog price, requested quantity, difference, and subtotal. Approve price and issue quote preserves the proposal unchanged; Amend price and issue quote requires an internal reason. Tax is system-calculated: include and freeze it when the billing and tax profile is complete and Finance-approved, or issue an explicitly pre-tax quote and calculate tax at invoicing. The issued quote, not the proposal, is the offer a Customer administrator may accept. The operational detail shows the current quote value, revision, and status. Internal context in the audit timeline explains Phaeno-only decisions; it is informational, not a Customer-facing warning. Assign an owner and due date when the workflow supports them. A queue assignment coordinates work; it does not grant authorization or change the workflow state.

sections.heading: Keep state boundaries visible
sections.text: Operational status, quote status, accounting-source readiness, payment, scientific readiness, file scanning, and publication are separate facts. Do not mark one complete merely because another succeeded. External users receive a limited timeline, so record a reason suitable for the affected Customer or Partner separately from internal notes whenever an action can be seen outside Phaeno. Order Ops ends at the Commercial boundary for a Customer laboratory order: it remains in Order intake while pricing and quote decisions are active. After acceptance and exact sample-roster finalization authorize that work, use Lab Ops for return-kit preparation, shipment-packet and tube comparison, specimen receipt and accession, protocol execution, materials, equipment, libraries, batches, sequencing sendouts, exceptions, and scientific approval. The PSeq kits and Assembly sections show the commercial record and link to their owning Lab Ops execution screen; the same physical action is recorded once. Lab readiness never publishes a file by itself.

sections.heading: Triage safely
sections.text: Confirm the active organization and workflow before opening a record. Review operational readiness, invitation delivery, scientific package, release, invoice, receipt, allocation, reconciliation, and notification states independently. Check open holds, cancellation requests, overdue actions, and failed deliveries. Assign the work and due date when ownership is unclear. Perform the smallest valid next action and preserve the existing record. POMS checks the latest Job immediately before issuing a quote. If the record changes after that check, POMS reloads it and preserves the entered quote lines; review those values, then issue the quote again. Never repair a failed workflow by creating a duplicate order, quote, invoice, receipt, result package, Lab work order, shipment, or release. Assign an attention item, preserve attempts, and record its resolution.

sections.heading: Review queued notifications
sections.text: Order notices check the current active organization, department, user, and administrator assignments when dispatched. The department notification address is included when configured; otherwise the organization notification default applies. An inactive or mismatched department cannot use either route. Review failed notices with no eligible recipients before retrying them; changing an assignment after a notice was queued changes who can receive it.

sections.heading: Use Finance
sections.text: Choose Invoices and aging, Receipts, Customer billing, Import receipts, or Reconciliation. A Customer filter carries into the record and back. Open the invoice, receipt, Customer, or batch number to review its details, then choose the relevant action. Editing happens in a dialog and errors retain the entered values. Invoice adjustments and receipt reversals retain a required reason. The dashboard summarizes recorded commercial and laboratory work and links to the owning screens. If data is unavailable, refresh or use the workspace directly; an unavailable count is not zero work.

guides.title: PSeq kit fulfillment
guides.summary: Review Partner kit orders commercially, then open Lab work for substitutions, backorders, and shipment fulfillment.

sections.heading: Partner reagent fulfillment
sections.text: Partner reagent orders use the offering and negotiated price available to the active Partner at placement. The placed order preserves an immutable Commercial snapshot even if catalog or pricing configuration changes later. Find the Commercial order in Order operations > PSeq kits. Perform the Commercial review and order acceptance there. After acceptance, perform physical preparation, substitutions, shipping, and fulfillment in Lab operations > PSeq kits. The Lab workflow consumes the Commercial snapshot; it does not rewrite the ordered items or negotiated price.

sections.heading: Review a placed order
sections.text: Confirm the Partner, purchase-order number, shipping address, ordered items, selling units, quantities, negotiated prices, currency, and placement totals. Verify that the shipping destination and requested service satisfy the configured restrictions. In Order operations, move valid work through review and acceptance. Reject it with a Partner-safe reason when the address, eligibility, quantity, or Commercial facts require correction. Keep internal investigation details in the internal record. Lab staff see the order as awaiting Commercial review and cannot start fulfillment until it is accepted.

sections.heading: Handle substitutions and backorders
sections.text: Never substitute a different reagent silently. Record the original item, proposed item, quantity, price effect, and reason. A Partner organization administrator or an administrator of the order's Department must explicitly approve the substitution. If the change increases the total, complete the required Commercial approval and preserve the adjustment for the manual accounting handoff before acceptance. Backorders remain part of the original order. Record the unshipped quantity and expected next action without changing quantities already shipped.

sections.heading: Create shipments
sections.text: Create a partial or complete shipment with: shipped quantities for each original order line; carrier, service, tracking number, and ship date; reagent lot or batch identifier; expiration date when the supplied reagent has one; and the packing-slip facts. Shipped quantities are immutable. Correct future fulfillment with a new shipment or documented adjustment; do not edit shipment history.

sections.heading: Complete fulfillment
sections.text: Reagent fulfillment creates a separate journal-entry source record for each shipment. Partial shipments therefore produce separate source rows tied to the same portal order. Finance completes invoice creation, account selection, tax treatment, and posting outside POMS. The order reaches fulfillment only when the accepted quantities are shipped, backordered quantities are resolved, and no blocking hold remains.

sections.heading: Move between Commercial and Lab work
sections.text: Use the Commercial order to accept or reject the kit order and decide Partner-facing changes or cancellation. Choose Open Lab work to prepare, substitute, ship, and complete the kit. The same order identity and history remain visible on both sides; fulfillment actions appear only in Lab operations.

guides.title: Company access and user administration
guides.summary: Manage Company access, staged Department readiness, service entitlements, invitations, and membership lifecycle.

sections.heading: Company access and user administration
sections.text: Phaeno administrators manage Portal access, readiness, service entitlements, integration requests, and global access from the canonical CRM Company. Prospect, Customer, and Partner administrators manage membership only within their own access scope. Access is invitation-based and every durable administrative change is audited.

sections.heading: Know which administration surface owns each record
sections.text: The CRM Companies directory is the only customer directory. A Company may exist before Portal access is approved. After approval, the same Company workspace displays its relationship type, readiness, services, members, invitations, requests, and retention settings. The internal Organization identifier used for tenant isolation is not a second customer record and does not appear in a separate directory. User management is also connected to durable account APIs. In the Phaeno context, active accounts and invited people appear in one list alongside global account status and every enforced Phaeno role. A Pending invitation status means the invitation has not been accepted and has not activated the offered access; the person may already have a sign-in account. Open a card’s actions menu to edit an active user, deactivate another active user, reactivate a disabled user, or resend or revoke a pending invitation. A Phaeno administrator cannot deactivate their own account. Edit one active user to update their name, Platform administrator assignment, and additive laboratory roles together. Platform administrators retain bootstrap access to every laboratory capability even when no explicit laboratory role is assigned. The role picker contains only roles enforced by the current authorization model: Platform administrator, Lab operator, Lab supervisor, Protocol administrator, Scientific reviewer, and Lab operations administrator. Authentication-provider metadata and unsupported job-title labels do not grant Portal access. Cards marked Pending invitation still represent invitation records, not accepted user records. Enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, then select the Platform administrator and additive laboratory roles they should receive. The pending role intent grants no access. It becomes active only when the recipient accepts and becomes an active Phaeno member.

sections.heading: Review and maintain Companies
sections.text: Create the Company first, then request the approved Portal relationship when access is needed: Prospect for an external organization that may receive explicitly granted curated data or participate in an approved no-charge Trial, but cannot place paid orders. Customer for organizations that request laboratory services. Partner for organizations that submit specimens for PSeq Lab Service or purchase the PSeq Kit, which includes data assembly. Internal employee invitations use the existing Phaeno organization in User management; Company requests create only the approved external relationship. Do not use Company lifecycle or Portal readiness as a shortcut for access. Curated package access requires an exact-version grant, member access requires an accepted invitation, and commercial work requires a current service entitlement. Open CRM and select Companies to search durable external customer records. Select the Company name to open its workspace. Use its Requests tab to propose online access, a product or service change, a relationship change, or reviewed work. Use CRM's central Requests section for requests that still need a Phaeno decision. The Company tab preserves request history but does not duplicate the decision controls. There is no standalone customer-creation action outside CRM. For a pending onboarding or evaluation request, select Approve and enable Portal access and record the approval reason. POMS atomically approves the request, creates the Company's internal tenant scope with Pending readiness, and attaches it to the existing Company. Online-access approval never adds or removes a product or service entitlement, creates another customer record, or creates a user. If an older approved onboarding or evaluation request shows Portal access incomplete, select Complete Portal access. POMS creates and attaches the missing tenant scope without changing product or service entitlements. This recovery does not create another Company, invite users, create an order, or complete the request. If POMS finds an active, compatible access scope with the exact Company name that is not linked to another Company, it pauses and shows Existing access scope found. Review the displayed name and relationship, then select Use existing access scope to reconnect it. Reuse preserves existing users, orders, invitations, and history. Existing Company requests are attached to the scope so they can be fulfilled through their separate owning workflows; attaching them does not grant product or service access. POMS will not offer this shortcut when the scope is inactive, belongs to another Company, or has a different relationship kind; resolve those cases before approving access. For a Customer, open Departments & services and choose the Department in Department readiness. The same derived checks used by Order Intake separate requirements before pricing, quote issuance, and invoicing. Follow each setup link to its owning screen. Historical readiness notes are retained as context; no manually selected Ready label authorizes work.

sections.heading: Review Company requests
sections.text: Use CRM's central Requests section to decide pending onboarding, evaluation, product and service, relationship, sales-assisted order, and offboarding requests created by the first-party CRM. Use Needs decision, Approved / needs work, and Completed / history to follow a request through completion. Approved requests stay actionable until completed or cancelled, and the Company's Requests tab links to the same queue. Historical imported requests remain readable alongside requests created in CRM; use the current queue to review their recorded state and available actions. Approve or decline a pending request with a reason. For onboarding or evaluation, approval also creates and attaches the Company's pending-readiness access scope while leaving product and service entitlements unchanged. Other request types record the decision only. Complete each approved invitation, entitlement, or order change through its owning workflow, verify the outcome, and then select Complete request in the central Requests queue and record what was completed. Never put specimen, scientific, downstream-customer, credential, or other sensitive operational details in an external reference or request summary.

sections.heading: Invite administrators and members
sections.text: From Company detail, open People. Use New person to create and associate a Contact in one save, or Add existing person to associate an existing Contact. Select Invite to Portal and choose Organization administrator or explicit Department membership and Department-admin roles. The Contact identity is filled in; edit the Contact first if its email or name is incorrect. Assign organization-wide administrator access only when the person must govern every Department; otherwise use Department membership and grant Department administrator access only where needed. A CRM Contact remains separate from a Portal user and grants no access until the invitation is accepted. Ask the recipient to sign in with the invited email and accept the Portal invitation. Use Manage access on the person to change their Organization role, add or remove Department access, change Department-admin roles, deactivate membership, and resend or revoke a pending invitation. Each change identifies the person and consequence before confirmation. Use Edit relationship to change their Company-specific title, commercial role, or effective dates. Use Departments & services to create or rename operational units, choose the default, and record typed configuration overrides. Every Organization begins with General. Organization administrators can edit the five Organization defaults for PO, billing and notification email, shipping, and result instructions. A blank Department override inherits the Organization default, then the commercial profile or system rule. The system PO rule is not required; either level can explicitly require or waive it. Existing saved shipping and accepted-quote snapshots retain their values. Result-delivery instructions are retained with the commercial commitment, not an automatic change to storage destinations. Organization administrators can access every active Department; other users must retain at least one active Department assignment. When one business unit must not be discoverable or governed by another—or it has separate contracting, tax, legal, ownership, or retention obligations—create a separate Company/Organization instead of a Department. External Organization and Department administrators can use Departments in the user menu. Organization administrators own structure, default selection, lifecycle, organization defaults, new invitations, and organization roles. Department administrators own settings and member access only within assigned Departments. Add existing members by exact email lookup; review each assignment or role change. One person may administer Research, belong to Operations as a member, and have no Finance access. Rights remain independent in each Organization. Department changes use review dialogs. Deactivation requires affected active members to have another Department assignment and retains historical records. Reactivation does not restore revoked assignments automatically. Changing the default affects future default selections, not existing records or memberships. A conflict reloads the latest Department version while preserving your form entries for review. Contact invitation access must still be valid when the invitation is resent or accepted; if the Contact or Department changed, review and reissue the invitation. Service entitlements and curated-data packages may be organization-wide or limited to one Department. A Department-specific service entitlement takes precedence over the Organization default for that Department. In Data provisioning, choose an explicit access scope when assigning a package; users in other Departments cannot list or download that Department's grant. Users with more than one available Department select the working Department from the user menu. The header shows the Organization and Department currently in force. Do not rely on a browser URL or a previously opened page to establish access; the API validates both scopes on every protected operation. Do not create a normal membership directly. Invitation acceptance provides the user-facing consent point and the audit link between invitation, user, and membership. For an internal employee, select the Phaeno organization and open User management. Use Add Phaeno user, enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, and select the narrowest roles needed for their work. Grant Platform administrator only when platform-wide administration is required. The card remains marked Pending invitation until acceptance; afterward, open its actions menu and choose Edit whenever the profile or roles must change. To follow up before acceptance, find the card marked Pending invitation, open its actions menu, and choose Resend invitation. Resending rotates the private link and is subject to a cooldown. Revoke an invitation that should not be accepted.

sections.heading: Convert a Prospect
sections.text: In the Prospect Company’s Requests tab, create Change the relationship and choose Customer or Partner. The form shows the current relationship and records your requested target. A reviewer approves it in Needs decision, then selects Apply Customer relationship or Apply Partner relationship in Approved / needs work and records the completed work. Applying the approved request performs the conversion and completes the request together. Customer-to-Partner and Partner-to-Customer reclassification are not supported by this action. Conversion preserves the Company, internal access identifier, users, memberships, grants, and audit history. It does not create an order, assign broad data access, or configure prices automatically. After conversion, complete the applicable operational setup: analysis availability and the billing and tax profile for a Customer, or offerings, negotiated reagent pricing, assembly profiles, and Partner assembly credit for a Partner.

sections.heading: Manage service entitlements
sections.text: From the Company, open Departments & services, then select Services to record dated commercial permission: Customers may receive PSeq Lab Service. Partners may receive PSeq Lab Service and PSeq Kit. Prospects and Phaeno organizations do not receive commercial service entitlements. Set configuration to Pending, Ready, or Blocked. A service is usable only when its entitlement is effective and configuration is Ready. Overlapping periods for the same service are rejected. If a service already has a non-ended entitlement, select Edit on that entitlement instead of adding another overlapping period. Preserve the service and existing effective date unless the commercial authorization changed, set the current configuration, attach the eligible approved source request, and save. Editing updates the existing audited record; it does not create a duplicate. Ended historical entitlements remain read-only. Online access does not imply a product or service entitlement. Add a dated entitlement here only after the corresponding product or service authorization is approved. When the entitlement implements an approved Portal request, select that request as its source. The selector shows only approved or applied requests for this organization that include the selected service. Leave the source blank only for a documented manual exception; do not attach an onboarding-only request to a service entitlement. Use End now instead of deleting an entitlement. Review the consequence dialog and record why the entitlement is ending. The Portal retains and displays that reason with the ended entitlement. PSeq Kit includes kit fulfillment followed by data submission and assembly. Do not create a separate data-assembly entitlement or sell data assembly without the kit.

sections.heading: Deactivate and restore access
sections.text: Deactivate a membership in Company detail to remove one access relationship. Deactivate the Company when none of its memberships should be usable; this suspends its attached Portal access scope. Reactivating the Company restores that scope. Each action opens a consequence dialog; verify the named Company or person before confirming. A deactivated membership is restored through a fresh invitation and acceptance. When all Portal access for another person must stop, select Deactivate on that Phaeno user and confirm the named person. The account, memberships, assigned roles, and audit history remain, but the user immediately loses effective access. A Phaeno administrator cannot deactivate their own account. Use Reactivate to restore an authorized disabled account; then review its memberships and roles before considering access complete. Preserve historical records; do not delete users, memberships, or organizations to resolve access problems.

sections.heading: Triage access safely
sections.text: Confirm the person’s email, session state, selected organization, active membership, role, and organization status. Use record identifiers and audit events to trace changes. Do not ask for passwords, sign-in codes, invitation tokens, browser storage, or another tenant’s records. For a user who has lost both the authenticator and all one-time backup codes, verify the person's identity and organization through the approved support procedure. In Clerk, reset the user's MFA enrollments and revoke every active session. Record the administrative recovery without storing codes, authenticator secrets, or recovery links. Tell the user to sign in again and connect a new authenticator; required MFA keeps the session pending until enrollment is complete. An email request starts the review but is not sufficient by itself to authorize the reset. If two administrators update the same record, the portal can reject the stale action. Reload the latest version, review the intervening change, and then make a deliberate new update rather than overwriting it.

guides.title: Statuses and recovery
guides.summary: Find each owning workspace and recover readiness, Lab work, releases, Finance, notifications, and retained history.

sections.heading: Statuses and recovery
sections.text: Recover the failed step from the record that owns it. Company access, order pricing, laboratory work, scientific release, billing, notifications, and retention have separate lifecycles. Repeating a successful earlier action can create duplicate work without fixing the failure.

sections.heading: Find the owning workspace
sections.text: | Work needing attention | Where to continue | | --- | --- | | Company access, invitation, or relationship request | CRM → Companies → People or the central Requests queue. Use Approved / needs work for approved requests awaiting completion. | | Customer pricing, quote, hold, or cancellation | Order operations → Order intake, then the Job. New Customer order starts each order; it is not configuration. | | Trial scope, approvals, acceptance, allowance, or closure | Order operations → Trial projects, then the Trial. | | Partner reagent or Assembly commercial review | Order operations → PSeq kits or Assembly. Open Lab work continues fulfillment or execution. | | Package, tube match, accession, execution, or scientific exception | The linked record in Lab operations. | | Scientifically approved PSeq package awaiting publication | Order operations → Result release, then the package. | | PSeq invoice, receipt, allocation, or reconciliation | The appropriate tab in Order operations → Finance. | | Cross-workflow follow-up or failed notice | Order operations → Attention; follow the item to its record. | | Curated-package grants, quarantine, or governance | Data provisioning, separate from the Customer Job's results. | Check search, status, date, owner, and Department filters before creating another record. A failed load differs from an empty list. Active intake includes held work; use On hold to focus on it, or All orders and history for accepted and terminal records. Lists preserve filters when you return from a record.

sections.heading: Recover Company readiness
sections.text: Open the Company's Departments & services and select the affected Department in Department readiness. The same checks appear during New Customer order. Requirements are separated into before pricing, before quote issuance, and before invoicing. Follow the setup link beside the requirement; a historical readiness label does not satisfy it. An active Customer, effective Ready service entitlement, valid offering, and no operational block allow pricing to begin. Quote issuance also requires operational configuration and an active Customer organization administrator. Billing and Finance approval may follow acceptance but must be complete before invoicing. See Customer lab authorization.

sections.heading: Recover laboratory and release work
sections.text: Packet and tube matching identifies authorized work; it does not record receipt. Continue to the linked Lab work, Record receipt, then Confirm accession. Resolve an unmatched or unsafe item through the receipt exception process. Resolve blocked execution and scientific exceptions in Lab operations using the authorized role. Keep internal investigation detail separate from the Customer summary. If a milestone publication fails, retry the existing event where recovery is offered; do not recreate the authorization, approval, or Lab work order. Review the complete, checksummed, malware-clean package and scientific approval in Result release before publication. Payment, invoice balance, and Customer credit do not gate PSeq results. Partner Assembly retains its separate credit and payment-hold rules. See Scientific approval and Data assembly review. Do not mark rejected files clean or change an order status to bypass a file gate. Correct the storage or scanning issue for failed or unavailable scans. Use the owning release action to withdraw a package that must no longer be delivered.

sections.heading: Recover Finance and notifications
sections.text: Use Finance for native PSeq invoices, receipts, allocations, corrections, imports, and reconciliation. An export does not record payment or mark an invoice posted elsewhere. Partner reagent shipments and Assembly outputs retain separate commercial source records for the manual accounting handoff. Before retrying a receipt or import, check whether it succeeded. Correct changed import input and preview it again; only the operator who reviewed the preview can confirm it. A receipt is recorded from accepted evidence, not from a successful email or connector retry. See Billing, payment, and release. Failed notifications do not reverse the underlying action. Correct eligible recipients or delivery issues and retry the existing notice where offered. For a hard-bounced invitation, use Company People to revoke it and issue a new invitation to the corrected Contact address. A queued recovery request is not proof of delivery or an available accounting connector.

sections.heading: Respect retained history
sections.text: Expired quotes require a current quote. Cancelled work, closed Trials, withdrawn files, completed Tasks, and expired downloads retain their history; follow the applicable new request, replacement, reissue, or correction workflow. Retention holds preserve or quarantine a release without extending its dates. Escalate with the record number, status, safe error, time, and action attempted. Keep credentials, invitation tokens, patient identifiers, investigations, and scientific files out of ordinary support notes.

guides.title: Trial Projects
guides.summary: Configure authorities and deliverables, approve scope, oversee samples and Lab work, release results, and close Trials.

sections.heading: Operate Trial Projects
sections.text: Trial Projects provide no-charge, closed-ended PSeq evaluations of extracted RNA. POMS owns the scientific scope, approvals, sample authorization, laboratory execution, and release. CRM owns the commercial request and follow-up. Trial work creates no order, quote, invoice, payment gate, or QuickBooks transaction. For Research Use Only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures. Never request PHI. Use coded sample references, and keep suspected prohibited information out of ordinary notes, notifications, and CRM summaries. Place affected Trial work on hold and follow the authorized incident process when prohibited information is suspected.

sections.heading: Find Trial projects
sections.text: Open Order ops, then choose Trial projects in the workspace sidebar. Search by Trial number or company, filter by status or Sales owner, and use Clear all to reset the list. An empty list is shown separately from a search with no matches. Select a Trial number to open its workspace; existing Trial links continue to work.

sections.heading: Prepare the commercial request and scope
